# Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

> Vanilla Breeze is an HTML-first component system. Native HTML elements are styled with no classes, layout comes from `data-layout` attributes, and custom elements add behaviour on top of markup that already works without JavaScript. There is no build step.

## Load it

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/vanilla-breeze@0.7.4/dist/cdn/vanilla-breeze.css">
<script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/vanilla-breeze@0.7.4/dist/cdn/vanilla-breeze.js"></script>
```

With npm: `npm install vanilla-breeze`, then `import 'vanilla-breeze/css'` and `import 'vanilla-breeze'`.

## Rules for writing markup

1. **Write complete native HTML first.** Use `header`, `nav`, `main`, `article`, `section`, `aside`, `footer`, headings in order, `label` with every form control. The page must be readable and usable before any Vanilla Breeze element or script is involved.
2. **Build page sections from the patterns.** The header and navigation, hero, feature grid, testimonial, call to action, pricing, FAQ, forms and footer each have a pattern file below with working markup. Start from the pattern; do not design these from scratch. A bare `<nav><ul>` is a vertical list: the navbar pattern shows `header.site` and `nav.horizontal`.
3. **Give content a width.** Put `data-layout="center"` (with `data-layout-max="narrow"`, `"normal"` or `"wide"`) on each top-level section inside `main`, or on `main` itself, so text does not run edge to edge. A full-width band such as a hero keeps its background on the outer element and centres an inner one.
4. **Do not use `<div>` or `<span>` for layout.** Put `data-layout` on a semantic element, or use a `layout-*` element where no semantic element fits. Layout values: `center`, `cluster`, `columns`, `cover`, `grid`, `media`, `page-stack`, `prose`, `reel`, `regions`, `sidebar`, `sidebar-left`, `sidebar-right`, `split`, `stack`, `switcher`.
5. **Attributes carry state and configuration.** Use the `data-*` attributes listed for a layout or component, with the values listed. Never invent a tag, an attribute or a value: if it is not in these files, it does not exist.
6. **Classes are a short documented vocabulary, not utilities.** Vanilla Breeze defines a few named variants, such as `header.site`, `nav.horizontal`, `section.hero`, `p.lead`, `a.button`, `button.secondary` and `button.ghost`. Use the ones the patterns and component files show. Do not invent utility classes, and do not use a class for state.
7. **Custom elements wrap working markup.** A component's children are its fallback: `<tab-set>` and `<accordion-wc>` wrap `<details>`, `<form-field>` wraps a `label` and an `input`. Never leave a component empty and expect script to fill it.
8. **Use `<form-field>` for form controls and `<icon-wc name="…">` for icons**, not hand-written wrappers or inline SVG.
9. **Choose a theme.** Set `data-theme` on `<html>` from `themes.md` to suit the content (and `data-accent` for brand hues); `data-mode="light"` or `"dark"` forces a colour scheme. An unthemed page works but looks generic.
10. **Style with a stylesheet and tokens, never inline.** No `style` attributes. When a pattern includes CSS, or the page needs a rule of its own (a hero background, a highlighted card), put it in a `<style>` block or a stylesheet and use design tokens such as `var(--color-primary)` and `var(--size-l)`, not literal colours or lengths. Keep it small: if you are writing layout CSS, there is a layout attribute for it.

## Check your work

Run the checker on every file you write or change, and fix everything it reports before you finish:

```bash
npx vb-check page.html
```

It needs `html-validate` installed beside `vanilla-breeze` (`npm install --save-dev html-validate`). It lists each problem with file, line, rule and the fix: unknown elements, attribute values that do not exist, `<div>` used for layout, inline styles, layout attributes no layout reads. An error means the markup is wrong; a warning asks you to confirm an attribute or class is intentional.

The checker reads markup. It cannot tell you the page looks right, so look at the rendered page as well when you can.

## How to use these files

Read the pattern file for each section of the page you are building, then the component file for each component those patterns use; a component file has the allowed attributes, values, child structure, events and keyboard behaviour, plus an example. `themes.md` lists the themes and the tokens to style with, `attributes.md` the attributes that work on any element, `native-elements.md` the native elements with dedicated documentation, and `llms-full.txt` holds everything in one file.

## Page patterns (start here for a page section)

- [Chat](patterns/application-chat.md): Chat integration patterns: floating launcher, embedded with sidebar, and full-page layouts using existing VB primitives.
- [Dashboard](patterns/application-dashboard.md): Dashboard layouts with stat cards, charts, and data tables. Build comprehensive admin interfaces and analytics views.
- [Profile](patterns/application-profile.md): User profile patterns with avatar displays, stats, activity feeds, and action buttons. Build profile pages and user cards for your applications.
- [Settings](patterns/application-settings.md): Settings page patterns with grouped sections, sidebar navigation, and tabbed interfaces for application preferences and configuration.
- [App Shells](patterns/application-shells.md): Application shell layouts for web apps, dashboards, and admin interfaces. Header, sidebar, and content area patterns.
- [Content Feed](patterns/data-content-feed.md): Filter + sort + paginated card list — the classic blog/product/search-results layout assembled from existing VB primitives. No content-feed component required.
- [Description List](patterns/data-description-list.md): Display key-value pairs using semantic HTML description lists. Perfect for detail panels, settings displays, and profile information.
- [File Display](patterns/data-files.md): Render uploaded or downloadable files as accessible rows, links, or cards. Uses [data-file] with icon-wc, native download links, and optional status/actions.
- [Stats](patterns/data-stats.md): Metric cards and stat displays with numbers, labels, and change indicators. Perfect for dashboards and data summaries.
- [Timeline](patterns/data-timeline.md): Vertical and horizontal timeline displays for chronological events, status tracking, and activity feeds. Perfect for order tracking, project history, and notifications.
- [Empty States](patterns/feedback-empty-states.md): Empty state patterns for when there's no content to display. State-driven feedback with semantic HTML.
- [Error Pages](patterns/feedback-error-pages.md): Error page patterns for 404, 500, and maintenance states. Guide users with clear messaging and helpful actions.
- [Skeleton](patterns/feedback-skeleton.md): Skeleton loading patterns to display placeholder content while data is being fetched. Reduce perceived load time with animated placeholders.
- [Checkout Form](patterns/forms-checkout.md): Checkout form patterns with single-page, split layout, and multi-step flows. Accessible and secure payment form designs.
- [Contact Form](patterns/forms-contact.md): Contact form patterns with split layouts, contact information sidebars, and map integration. Accessible and responsive designs for customer communication.
- [Registration](patterns/forms-registration.md): Sign up form patterns with multi-step flows, social authentication, and password requirements. Accessible and progressively enhanced.
- [Sign In](patterns/forms-sign-in.md): Login form patterns with social authentication, two-factor input, and responsive layouts. Accessible and progressively enhanced.
- [Wizard / Multi-Step Form](patterns/forms-wizard.md): Multi-step form patterns with numbered steps, tab navigation, and progress bar indicators. Guide users through complex forms with clear progress feedback.
- [Call to Action](patterns/marketing-cta.md): Call to action section patterns for landing pages and marketing sites. Centered banners, split layouts, and background image CTAs.
- [FAQ](patterns/marketing-faq.md): FAQ section patterns for landing pages and marketing sites. Accordion, grid, and categorized layouts for displaying frequently asked questions.
- [Feature](patterns/marketing-features.md): Feature section patterns for marketing sites. Icon grids, alternating layouts, card grids, and feature highlights.
- [Hero](patterns/marketing-hero.md): Hero section patterns for landing pages and marketing sites. Centered text, split layouts, background images, forms, and video backgrounds.
- [Pricing](patterns/marketing-pricing.md): Pricing section patterns for SaaS and product landing pages. Tiered cards, feature comparison tables, and billing toggle options.
- [Testimonial](patterns/marketing-testimonials.md): Testimonial section patterns for landing pages and marketing sites. Quote cards, avatar grids, and carousel layouts.
- [Breadcrumb](patterns/navigation-breadcrumb.md): Breadcrumb navigation helps users understand their location within a site hierarchy and provides quick access to parent pages. Built with semantic HTML and accessible by default.
- [Footer](patterns/navigation-footer.md): Footer navigation patterns with links, social icons, multi-column layouts, and newsletter signup forms.
- [Navbar](patterns/navigation-navbar.md): Header navigation patterns with dropdowns, search, and mobile responsive menus.
- [Pagination](patterns/navigation-pagination.md): Page navigation patterns for multi-page content, tables, and search results.
- [Sidebar Navigation](patterns/navigation-sidebar.md): Vertical sidebar navigation patterns with icons, sections, and collapsible groups.
- [Step Indicator](patterns/navigation-steps.md): Step indicators show progress through a multi-step process. Built with CSS counters for auto-numbering, auto-generated connectors, and ARIA attributes for accessibility.
- [Scroll-Down Indicator](patterns/scroll-scroll-down-indicator.md): Animated chevron at the bottom of a hero nudging readers to scroll. Pure CSS, reduced-motion aware.
- [Sticky Hero with Scale-Out](patterns/scroll-sticky-hero.md): Pinned hero that scales and fades as the reader scrolls past. Pure CSS via position: sticky + animation-timeline: view().
- [Sticky Share Bar](patterns/scroll-sticky-share-bar.md): Vertical share rail beside an article that follows the reader. Pure position: sticky composition, no JS, no scroll listeners.

## Layouts

- [<layout-badge>](components/layout-badge.md): Small inline status or count badge.
- [<layout-canvas>](components/layout-canvas.md): Elevated content surface (a panel with radius, shadow and a 1px edge: a hairline on a plain page, transparent under data-backdrop, CanvasText in forced colours).
- [<layout-card>](components/layout-card.md): Card surface.
- [<layout-center>](components/layout-center.md): Horizontally centered, max-width-constrained container with side gutters.
- [<layout-cluster>](components/layout-cluster.md): Horizontal wrapping flex row for groups of short items — tags, buttons, metadata.
- [<layout-columns>](components/layout-columns.md): Multi-column text flow with a readable measure, vertical rhythm (between direct children), column rules and break hygiene.
- [<layout-cover>](components/layout-cover.md): Full-height (min-block-size) flex column that vertically centers a principal element (data-layout-principal; a sole child auto-centers), with header/footer or cover-top/-bottom children pinned to the edges.
- [<layout-grid>](components/layout-grid.md): Auto-fit responsive grid: as many columns as fit the minimum width, then wrap.
- [<layout-imposter>](components/layout-imposter.md): Positioned overlay centred over (or pinned to an edge or corner of) its containing block, logically (mirrored in RTL).
- [<layout-reel>](components/layout-reel.md): Horizontal scrolling strip with proximity snap points, an optional scrollbar and edge hints.
- [<layout-sidebar>](components/layout-sidebar.md): Two-column layout: a fixed-basis sidebar beside a flexible content column that wraps below it when there is no room.
- [<layout-stack>](components/layout-stack.md): Vertical flex stack with a consistent gap between children.
- [<layout-switcher>](components/layout-switcher.md): Flex row that switches to a column once the switcher's own width drops below the threshold (a flex-basis formula, no media or container query).
- [<layout-text>](components/layout-text.md): Long-form reading container: a readable measure plus vertical rhythm between direct children.

## Web components (need the script; children are the fallback)

- [<accordion-wc>](components/accordion-wc.md): Accordion built on native details/summary with exclusive mode and transitions
- [<activity-feed>](components/activity-feed.md): WAI-ARIA Feed timeline of user actions.
- [<ai-chat>](components/ai-chat.md): On-device chat via Chrome's LanguageModel API.
- [<ai-summary>](components/ai-summary.md): Summarise wrapped content via Chrome's Summarizer API, with optional inline endpoint fallback and external deep-link fallback.
- [<analytics-panel>](components/analytics-panel.md): Visitor-facing view of what analytics is doing on this page: whether it runs, why it is off, and which fields an event carries, with a Pause / Resume control.
- [<audio-player>](components/audio-player.md): Platform audio player web component
- [<audio-visualizer>](components/audio-visualizer.md): Canvas-based audio visualization companion
- [<author-index>](components/author-index.md): Author-grouped view of site content.
- [<brand-mark>](components/brand-mark.md): Brand/logo display.
- [<bread-crumb>](components/bread-crumb.md): Hierarchical navigation trail.
- [<calendar-wc>](components/calendar-wc.md): Standalone calendar display with rich cell content
- [<card-list>](components/card-list.md): Template-based list rendering with safe data binding: property paths only, sanitized HTML, and URL-checked attribute bindings
- [<carousel-wc>](components/carousel-wc.md): Scrolling carousel with autoplay, looping, indicators, and view transitions
- [<change-set>](components/change-set.md): Interactive change tracking group: a caption from author/datetime plus Tracking / Final / Original toggles over its <ins> / <del> descendants
- [<chart-wc>](components/chart-wc.md): SVG chart component with progressive enhancement: semantic table → CSS chart → SVG chart.
- [<chat-input>](components/chat-input.md): Form-associated chat input with auto-growing textarea; submits its form, or fires chat-input:send when standalone
- [<chat-window>](components/chat-window.md): Light DOM orchestrator for chat UI
- [<color-picker>](components/color-picker.md): Form-associated color picker with saturation/lightness area, hue slider, HEX/RGB/HSL/OKLCH inputs, preset swatches, Copy and EyeDropper
- [<combo-box>](components/combo-box.md): Autocomplete combobox with filtering, keyboard navigation, and native form association
- [<command-group>](components/command-group.md): A labelled group of <command-item> elements inside a <command-palette>.
- [<command-item>](components/command-item.md): One command inside a <command-palette>, optionally within a <command-group>.
- [<command-palette>](components/command-palette.md): Command palette / Cmd+K launcher (modal dialog, combobox + listbox)
- [<comment-box>](components/comment-box.md): Form-associated comment form composing <markdown-editor> + Submit / Cancel buttons.
- [<comment-thread>](components/comment-thread.md): Persistent threaded-discussion container.
- [<comment-wc>](components/comment-wc.md): EXPERIMENTAL / STUB: inline "Add comment" action for selection-menu.
- [<compare-surface>](components/compare-surface.md): Before/after comparison slider: two overlaid children with a draggable, keyboard-operable divider (side by side without JS)
- [<consent-banner>](components/consent-banner.md): Cookie consent banner with granular category controls and persistence
- [<content-lens>](components/content-lens.md): Universal switchable host for VB lens components; JS API: activeLens (read-only), setLens(name)
- [<content-swap>](components/content-swap.md): Two-face content toggle with accessible state management.
- [<context-menu>](components/context-menu.md): Right-click (and Shift+F10 / ContextMenu key) menu with keyboard navigation and shortcut bindings
- [<data-table>](components/data-table.md): Enhanced HTML table with sorting, filtering, pagination, row expansion, and selection
- [<date-picker>](components/date-picker.md): Form-associated calendar date picker with combobox text entry
- [<day-view>](components/day-view.md): Hour-grid schedule for a single day, using hour-view and calendar-event children
- [<diagram-wc>](components/diagram-wc.md): Declarative diagram renderer — wraps Mermaid (v1) with VB token-driven theming, lazy load, and HTML-first authoring via fenced code blocks
- [<drag-surface>](components/drag-surface.md): Accessible drag-and-drop reorder surface with keyboard reorder, optional single-pointer move controls, live announcements and cross-surface transfer
- [<drop-down>](components/drop-down.md): Accessible dropdown: an APG menu button for actions, or (with hover) an APG disclosure for navigation links
- [<emoji-picker>](components/emoji-picker.md): Accessible emoji picker with search, a category toolbar, a listbox of emoji, and undoable insertion into a target field
- [<flow-diagram>](components/flow-diagram.md): User flow and sequence visualization — progressively enhances an ol into a labelled figure holding a nested list drawn as a connected node graph with actions, decisions, and branches
- [<foot-note>](components/foot-note.md): One footnote, written inline where its reference mark belongs.
- [<foot-notes>](components/foot-notes.md): Progressive enhancement for footnotes: collects the <foot-note> elements that precede it into a labelled doc-endnotes list (or margin sidenotes), with doc-noteref references, doc-backlink return links, shared notes for repeat citations and a hover/focus preview.
- [<form-field>](components/form-field.md): Accessible form field: binds its control (native or form-associated custom element), times validation, shows hint/error outputs and wires aria-describedby / aria-invalid
- [<geo-map>](components/geo-map.md): A zero-dependency map component using OpenStreetMap / CARTO raster tiles or your own tile proxy, with a lazy-loaded interactive pan / zoom mode.
- [<glossary-index>](components/glossary-index.md): Interactive glossary with search filtering and scroll-spy letter tracking; copyable term permalinks are opt-in
- [<glossary-wc>](components/glossary-wc.md): Searchable, categorized, cross-linked glossary that progressively enhances a definition list
- [<heading-links>](components/heading-links.md): Add permalink anchors to headings; activating one follows the fragment and copies the section URL
- [<highlight-wc>](components/highlight-wc.md): Text highlighting with localStorage persistence.
- [<icon-wc>](components/icon-wc.md): Inline SVG icon: fetches one sanitized SVG file per icon from <base-path>/<set>/<name>.svg, sized by preset and labelled for assistive tech
- [<image-gallery>](components/image-gallery.md): Thumbnail grid with lightbox viewer.
- [<image-map>](components/image-map.md): Responsive image map: <map-area> children define percentage-coordinate hotspots (rect, circle, poly) over a child <img>, with an SVG hit-testing overlay, keyboard-focusable anchors, and rich HTML tooltips.
- [<include-file>](components/include-file.md): Fetch a same-origin HTML fragment, sanitize it, and insert it into the page
- [<markdown-editor>](components/markdown-editor.md): Side-by-side markdown editor with live preview.
- [<markdown-viewer>](components/markdown-viewer.md): Render markdown content with progressive enhancement.
- [<nav-bar>](components/nav-bar.md): Top-level site/app navigation primitive.
- [<note-wc>](components/note-wc.md): Private reader notes on highlights: a note action inside selection-menu, a page-level button with for="id", and the note panel itself.
- [<notification-wc>](components/notification-wc.md): Dual-mode notification component: dismissible banner or bell-icon panel with history + read tracking.

- [<page-stats>](components/page-stats.md): Lightweight reading statistics

- [<pager-wc>](components/pager-wc.md): Standalone pagination controls element targeting any [data-paged] container.

- [<recently-visited>](components/recently-visited.md): Device-local reader history lens (localStorage, never sent or aggregated).
- [<score-card>](components/score-card.md): Single KPI tile for dashboards: title, headline value, optional change indicator, sparkline (composed with <chart-wc>), description, and icon.

- [<settings-panel>](components/settings-panel.md): Compact, non-modal site settings panel (Appearance, Accessibility, Layout, Effects, Environment, System) opened from a gear trigger; shares state with theme-picker through ThemeManager, VBStore and window events
- [<share-wc>](components/share-wc.md): Social share component: native Web Share button (falls back to copying the link), platform buttons, or enhanced slotted links; inside selection-menu, shares or copies the selected text as a quote.
- [<short-cuts>](components/short-cuts.md): Keyboard shortcuts help overlay: a modal dialog listing the command registry ([data-command][data-shortcut]) and data-hotkey actions, toggled by ? (remappable or off) or show()/toggle().
- [<site-index>](components/site-index.md): Interactive keyword index: one filter box, an A–Z jump strip, a term count per letter and an optional display limit over a hand-authored (or src JSON) index
- [<site-map>](components/site-map.md): Dual-mode sitemap: a lightweight static-sitemap enhancer (nav-enhance) or an interactive information-architecture tree with badges and an org-chart visual mode (ia-tree)
- [<site-search>](components/site-search.md): Pagefind-powered site search in a native modal <dialog>: combobox input, listbox of results, live result count
- [<slide-accept>](components/slide-accept.md): Slide-to-confirm interaction.
- [<social-embed>](components/social-embed.md): Privacy-first social post embed.

- [<social-links>](components/social-links.md): A row of profile links.

- [<star-rating>](components/star-rating.md): Form-associated star rating web component: generates a fieldset[data-rating] of radios (CSS layer) opted into the rating effect (clear, rating:change), and submits one name=value entry via ElementInternals.
- [<status-wc>](components/status-wc.md): Visual state indicator.
- [<stepper-wc>](components/stepper-wc.md): Stepper for values <input type="number"> + data-stepper cannot reach: formatted units, currency, time, token-snap scales, discrete enums.
- [<tab-set>](components/tab-set.md): Tab container built on native details/summary with keyboard navigation and view transitions
- [<text-reader>](components/text-reader.md): Text-to-speech reader with word-level highlighting (Web Speech API + CSS Custom Highlight API)
- [<theme-picker>](components/theme-picker.md): Theme selection: color mode and theme (a select of every theme, or a short list as swatches), as a popover or inline panel
- [<time-index>](components/time-index.md): Interactive changelog/timeline component: relative dates, an order select, a version filter and a recently-updated-pages feed
- [<time-picker>](components/time-picker.md): Form-associated time input with combobox text entry and a spinbutton popup
- [<toast-msg>](components/toast-msg.md): Toast notification stack: one polite live region, queued toasts beyond max, auto-dismiss that pauses on hover/focus, localisable labels
- [<tool-tip>](components/tool-tip.md): Tooltip or hover card composed on <pop-over>: hover/focus with delay, interestfor where available, Escape and outside dismiss
- [<topic-map>](components/topic-map.md): SKOS-aware hierarchical view of site concepts.
- [<trust-filter>](components/trust-filter.md): Provenance lens: filter pages.json by vb:provenance, vb:review, vb:status and whether a signature is declared (not verified).
- [<version-switcher>](components/version-switcher.md): Surface and switch between versions of a page over time.
- [<video-player>](components/video-player.md): Platform video player: custom, keyboard-accessible controls (shadow DOM) over a light-DOM <video>, with optional playlist
- [<watch-wc>](components/watch-wc.md): Drop-in wrapper for the data-watch-page button.
- [<week-view>](components/week-view.md): Week time grid composing day-view-style columns in a semantic table.
- [<youtube-player>](components/youtube-player.md): YouTube embed behind a facade: a thumbnail (or local poster) and one play button; the youtube-nocookie.com iframe loads only when the reader presses play.

## CSS-only elements

- [<calendar-event>](components/calendar-event.md): CSS-only event block for <day-view>, <week-view> and the <calendar-wc> day detail: category colour, inline-start accent bar, half-hour placement.
- [<chat-bubble>](components/chat-bubble.md): Content wrapper for chat messages with typography, code block styling, and CSS-only typing dots animation.
- [<chat-message>](components/chat-message.md): A single chat turn with role-based alignment, optional avatar support, sender metadata, and message state indicators.
- [<chat-thread>](components/chat-thread.md): Scrollable message container for chat conversations.
- [<dl>](components/dl.md): The description list element represents a collection of term-description pairs, such as glossaries, metadata, or key-value data.
- [<fab-stack>](components/fab-stack.md): Fixed action button stack.
- [<hour-view>](components/hour-view.md): CSS-only container for calendar events within a single hour slot.
- [<loading-spinner>](components/loading-spinner.md): CSS-only animated loading spinner.
- [<mobile-menu>](components/mobile-menu.md): Breakpoint observer for a header menu.
- [<site-legal>](components/site-legal.md): Legal and compliance content container for copyright, license, privacy, and terms links
- [<site-tools>](components/site-tools.md): Site-wide utility container for header and footer actions like search, theme picker, and settings
- [<status-message>](components/status-message.md): Inline notification banners for important messages.
- [<table>](components/table.md): Tables display tabular data with full-width layout, collapsed borders, tabular numerals, and automatic row hover states.
- [<text-divider>](components/text-divider.md): Horizontal divider with centered text.
- [<user-avatar>](components/user-avatar.md): CSS-only avatar shell: a photo <img>, an initials / icon fallback stacked under it, and an optional presence dot.

## Separate packages (not in the bundle)

- [<browser-window>](components/browser-window.md): Safari-style browser window frame for demos and tutorials.
- [<code-block>](components/code-block.md): Code block with syntax highlighting, copy button, line numbers and themes.

## Reference

- [Themes](themes.md): Every theme and accent with a one-line character, how to load one, and the design tokens to use in your own rules
- [Attributes](attributes.md): Attributes that work on any element, grouped by purpose
- [Native elements](native-elements.md): Native elements with dedicated documentation

## Guides

- [Quick Start](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/quick-start/): One HTML file, ten minutes. Write plain semantic HTML, then add Vanilla Breeze one optional layer at a time: styles, layout attributes, components and a theme. No utility classes, no wrapper divs, no build step.
- [Principles](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/principles/): What Vanilla Breeze commits to: HTML as the atom, one grammar across HTML, CSS and JavaScript, optional layers, themeable presentation, minimal execution, overridable defaults and the web for all.
- [Semantic Layouts](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/semantic-layouts/): Put a layout on the element you already have with data-layout, and skip the wrapper. The rules are the same as the layout elements, with a few differences that come from the host element.
- [Layouts Overview](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/layouts/): How Vanilla Breeze arranges things on a page: a small set of layouts that each do one job, respond to the space they are given and nest inside each other.
- [Themes](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/themes/): Color themes and personality themes for Vanilla Breeze. Customize your design with a single attribute.
- [Design Tokens](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/tokens/): CSS custom properties for colors, spacing, typography, borders, shadows, and motion. Consistent values for your entire design system.
- [Accessibility Overview](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/accessibility/): What Vanilla Breeze does for accessibility, what you still provide, the standard it aims at and the checks that hold it there.

---

# Chat

Chat integration patterns: floating launcher, embedded with sidebar, and full-page layouts using existing VB primitives.

- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/patterns/application/chat/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Overview

These patterns compose `<chat-window>` with existing VB primitives to create complete chat experiences. No new custom elements are needed — `<dialog>`, `commandfor`, and `<layout-sidebar>` handle the shell.

## Floating Launcher

A fixed-position FAB button opens a `<dialog>` containing `chat-window`. The `commandfor`/`command` attributes handle open/close automatically with proper focus management.

Floating chat launcher:

```html
<style>
.chat-trigger {
  position: fixed;
  inset-block-end: var(--size-xl);
  inset-inline-end: var(--size-xl);
  z-index: 1000;
  width: 56px;
  height: 56px;
  border-radius: var(--radius-full);
  background: var(--color-primary);
  color: var(--color-text-on-primary);
  border: none;
  cursor: pointer;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  box-shadow: 0 4px 16px oklch(0% 0 0 / 0.2);
  transition: transform var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-default),
              box-shadow var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-default);
}
.chat-trigger:hover {
  transform: scale(1.06);
  box-shadow: 0 6px 20px oklch(0% 0 0 / 0.28);
}
.chat-trigger:active { transform: scale(0.96); }
</style>

<!-- Fixed trigger button -->
<button commandfor="chat-dialog" command="show-modal"
        class="chat-trigger" aria-label="Open chat">
  <icon-wc name="message-circle"></icon-wc>
</button>

<!-- Dialog contains chat-window -->
<dialog id="chat-dialog">
  <chat-window endpoint="/api/chat">
    <script type="application/json" data-participants>
    { "user": { "name": "You", "role": "user" },
      "assistant": { "name": "Assistant", "role": "agent" } }
    </script>
    <header>
      <h3>AI Assistant</h3>
      <button commandfor="chat-dialog" command="close"
              class="ghost small" aria-label="Close">
        <icon-wc name="x"></icon-wc>
      </button>
    </header>
    <chat-thread role="log" aria-label="Chat" aria-live="polite">
    </chat-thread>
    <chat-input name="message">
      <textarea data-grow rows="1" placeholder="Ask anything..."></textarea>
      <footer>
        <button type="submit" class="small" data-send aria-label="Send">
          <icon-wc name="send"></icon-wc>
        </button>
      </footer>
    </chat-input>
  </chat-window>
</dialog>
```

## Unread Badge

Add an unread count using `<layout-badge>` positioned over the trigger button.

Trigger with unread badge:

```html
<button commandfor="chat-dialog" command="show-modal"
        class="chat-trigger" aria-label="Open chat">
  <icon-wc name="message-circle"></icon-wc>
  <layout-badge data-color="error" data-size="s">3</layout-badge>
</button>
```

Position the badge over the trigger:

```css
.chat-trigger {
  position: relative;
}

.chat-trigger layout-badge {
  position: absolute;
  inset-block-start: calc(-1 * var(--size-2xs));
  inset-inline-end: calc(-1 * var(--size-2xs));
}
```

## Embedded with Sidebar

For always-visible chat panels, use `<layout-sidebar>` with a chat history list in the aside. The sidebar collapses on narrow viewports.

Embedded chat with sidebar:

```html
<layout-sidebar data-layout-sidebar-width="narrow">
  <aside>
    <nav aria-label="Chat history">
      <a href="/chat/5" aria-current="true">Current conversation</a>
      <a href="/chat/4">Refund request</a>
      <a href="/chat/3">Setup help</a>
    </nav>
  </aside>
  <chat-window endpoint="/api/ai">
    <script type="application/json" data-participants>
    { "user": { "name": "You", "role": "user" },
      "assistant": { "name": "Assistant", "role": "agent" } }
    </script>
    <header>
      <h3>Support Chat</h3>
    </header>
    <chat-thread role="log" aria-label="Support conversation" aria-live="polite">
    </chat-thread>
    <chat-input name="message">
      <textarea data-grow rows="1" placeholder="Type a message..."></textarea>
      <footer>
        <button type="submit" class="small" data-send aria-label="Send">
          <icon-wc name="send"></icon-wc>
        </button>
      </footer>
    </chat-input>
  </chat-window>
</layout-sidebar>
```

## Full-Page with History Drawer

A full-viewport chat: give the window `block-size: 100dvh` in your stylesheet. The history drawer uses `<dialog data-position="start">` for a slide-in panel triggered from the header.

Full-page chat:

```html
<chat-window endpoint="/api/ai" class="full-page">
  <script type="application/json" data-participants>
  { "user": { "name": "You", "role": "user" },
    "assistant": { "name": "Assistant", "role": "agent" } }
  </script>
  <header>
    <button commandfor="chat-history" command="show-modal"
            class="ghost small" aria-label="History">
      <icon-wc name="sidebar"></icon-wc>
    </button>
    <h3>Chat</h3>
    <select data-model-select aria-label="Select model">
      <option value="claude-sonnet-4-6">Sonnet 4.6</option>
      <option value="claude-haiku-4-5">Haiku 4.5</option>
    </select>
  </header>
  <chat-thread role="log" aria-label="Conversation" aria-live="polite">
  </chat-thread>
  <chat-input name="message">
    <textarea data-grow rows="1" data-max-rows="8"
              placeholder="Ask anything..."></textarea>
    <footer>
      <button type="submit" class="small" data-send aria-label="Send">
        <icon-wc name="send"></icon-wc>
      </button>
    </footer>
  </chat-input>
</chat-window>

<dialog id="chat-history" data-position="start">
  <header>
    <h3>History</h3>
    <button commandfor="chat-history" command="close" class="ghost small" aria-label="Close history">
      <icon-wc name="x"></icon-wc>
    </button>
  </header>
  <nav aria-label="Previous conversations">
    <a href="/chat/5" aria-current="true">Current conversation</a>
    <a href="/chat/4">Refund request</a>
    <a href="/chat/3">Setup help</a>
  </nav>
</dialog>
```

Fill the viewport:

```css
chat-window.full-page {
  block-size: 100dvh;
}
```

## Related

- `<chat-window>` — The orchestrating web component
- `<chat-input>` — Form-associated input
- `<chat-thread>` — Scrollable message container
- `<dialog>` — Native modal/drawer
- `<layout-sidebar>` — Split panel layout

# Dashboard

Dashboard layouts with stat cards, charts, and data tables. Build comprehensive admin interfaces and analytics views.

- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/patterns/application/dashboard/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Overview

Dashboard patterns combine multiple components to create data-rich interfaces. These layouts organize statistics, visualizations, and tabular data in a way that's easy to scan and understand.

Key features:
- KPI tiles with `<score-card>`: title, value, change, sparkline and icon slots, coloured by `trend`
- Charts with `<chart-wc>`, sized by a responsive grid
- Native `<table>` styling inside `<data-table>`, with `<layout-badge>` for status and `<user-avatar>` for identity
- Responsive grid layouts using `data-layout-min` for automatic column sizing
- Consistent spacing and `<layout-card>`-based organization

## Stats Grid Dashboard

A dashboard focused on key metrics displayed in `<score-card>` tiles. Each tile slots a title, a `<data>` value, a `<small>` change line, a sparkline and an icon; `trend="up|down"` colours the change, and wrapping the tile in a link makes it a drill-down.

`<score-card>` styles its own tile. The page supplies two small rules: the stroke of an inline SVG sparkline, coloured by the card's trend, and the link wrapper that makes a tile clickable. Swap the SVG for `<chart-wc slot="sparkline" data-size="sparkline">` to drop the first rule.

dashboard-stats.html:

```html
<main data-layout="center" data-layout-max="wide" data-layout-gap="xl">
  <!-- Page Header -->
  <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between" data-layout-align="center">
    <hgroup>
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <p>Overview of your business metrics</p>
    </hgroup>
    <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s">
      <button type="button" class="button secondary">
        <icon-wc name="calendar" size="sm"></icon-wc>
        Last 30 days
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="button">
        <icon-wc name="download" size="sm"></icon-wc>
        Export
      </button>
    </layout-cluster>
  </header>

  <!-- Stats Grid -->
  <layout-grid data-layout-gap="l" data-layout-min="m">
    <a href="#revenue">
      <score-card trend="up" tone="success">
        <span slot="title">Total Revenue</span>
        <data slot="value" value="45231">$45,231</data>
        <small slot="change"><data value="0.12">+12%</data> from last month</small>
        <svg slot="sparkline" viewBox="0 0 100 30" preserveAspectRatio="none" role="img" aria-label="Revenue trend, increasing">
          <path d="M 0 22 L 20 19 L 40 17 L 60 12 L 80 8 L 100 4"/>
          <circle cx="100" cy="4" r="2"/>
        </svg>
        <icon-wc slot="icon" name="dollar-sign" size="md"></icon-wc>
      </score-card>
    </a>

    <a href="#tasks">
      <score-card trend="down" tone="warning">
        <span slot="title">Tasks Completed</span>
        <data slot="value" value="0.89">89%</data>
        <small slot="change"><data value="-0.04">-4%</data> from last month</small>
        <!-- sparkline… -->
        <icon-wc slot="icon" name="check-circle" size="md"></icon-wc>
      </score-card>
    </a>
    <!-- Additional score cards... -->
  </layout-grid>
</main>
```

Sparkline and link CSS:

```css
svg[slot="sparkline"]        { display: block; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; }
svg[slot="sparkline"] path   { fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2; vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke; }
svg[slot="sparkline"] circle { fill: currentColor; }
score-card[trend="up"]   [slot="sparkline"] { color: var(--color-success); }
score-card[trend="down"] [slot="sparkline"] { color: var(--color-error); }

a:has(score-card) {
  display: block;
  text-decoration: none;
  color: inherit;
  border-radius: var(--radius-m);
}
a:has(score-card):hover score-card {
  transform: translateY(-2px);
  border-color: var(--color-interactive);
}
```

## Charts Dashboard

An analytics layout: a row of `<score-card>` tiles above a responsive grid of `<layout-card>` panels, each holding a `<chart-wc>`. `<chart-wc>` ships in the separate charts bundle, so the page loads `vanilla-breeze-charts.css` and `vanilla-breeze-charts.js`.

## Data Table Dashboard

A dashboard centered on tabular data with a filter bar, status badges via `<layout-badge>`, user avatars via `<user-avatar>`, and row actions. The native `<table>` sits in `<data-table>`, whose container query lets `data-responsive="card"` turn rows into cards in a narrow card.

No extra CSS is needed. A button whose only child is an `<icon-wc>` and which carries an `aria-label` is squared automatically.

dashboard-table.html:

```html
<layout-card data-padding="none">
  <data-table>
    <table data-responsive="card">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">Customer</th>
          <th scope="col">Email</th>
          <th scope="col">Status</th>
          <th scope="col">Amount</th>
          <th scope="col">Date</th>
          <th scope="col">Actions</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td>
            <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s" data-layout-nowrap>
              <user-avatar data-size="sm">
                <span data-fallback>JD</span>
              </user-avatar>
              <span>John Doe</span>
            </layout-cluster>
          </td>
          <td>john.doe@example.com</td>
          <td>
            <layout-badge data-color="success" data-variant="subtle" data-size="l">Completed</layout-badge>
          </td>
          <td>$250.00</td>
          <td>Jan 15, 2026</td>
          <td>
            <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="xs" data-layout-nowrap>
              <button type="button" class="button ghost small" aria-label="View order">
                <icon-wc name="eye" size="sm"></icon-wc>
              </button>
              <button type="button" class="button ghost small" aria-label="Edit order">
                <icon-wc name="edit" size="sm"></icon-wc>
              </button>
              <button type="button" class="button ghost small" aria-label="More actions">
                <icon-wc name="more-vertical" size="sm"></icon-wc>
              </button>
            </layout-cluster>
          </td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </data-table>
</layout-card>
```

## Configuration

Dashboard patterns use these layout attributes and components:

## Usage Notes

- KPI tiles: `<score-card>` lays out its slots and colours the change by `trend`; put the number in `<data value>` so the raw value stays machine-readable
- Native tables: Vanilla Breeze styles `<table>` elements directly — no custom classes needed. Wrap the table in `<data-table>` and add `data-responsive="card"` to reflow rows on small screens, or use a `[data-table-scroll]` wrapper for horizontal scrolling.
- Loading states: Show skeleton placeholders while data loads to prevent layout shift
- Responsive layout: The grid automatically adjusts columns based on `data-layout-min`; test on mobile to ensure usability
- Charts: `<chart-wc>` reads `data-values` JSON or a child `<table>`; another library can render into the same `<layout-card>` slot instead
- Semantic colors: Use `--color-success` for positive trends, `--color-error` for negative
- Empty states: Provide helpful empty states when no data is available
- Accessibility: Ensure tables have proper `scope` attributes and buttons have `aria-label`
- Real-time updates: Consider using subtle animations when stats update dynamically

## Related

Application shell layouts with navigation

Stat card patterns and change indicators

Card component with padding and variant options

Status badges with semantic colors

Avatar component with fallback initials

SVG icon component with size variants

KPI tile with value, change and sparkline slots

SVG charts from JSON or a table

# Profile

User profile patterns with avatar displays, stats, activity feeds, and action buttons. Build profile pages and user cards for your applications.

- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/patterns/application/profile/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Overview

Profile patterns display user information in various contexts, from compact cards to full-page layouts. These patterns combine avatars, user data, statistics, and interactive elements into cohesive displays.

Key features:
- Avatar display with image or initials fallback
- `<hgroup>` for name + role pairs with automatic muted subtitle styling
- `<dl>` / `<dt>` / `<dd>` for stat label/value pairs — semantic and accessible
- Activity feeds showing recent actions
- Action buttons for messaging, following, and editing
- Responsive sidebar layout that automatically stacks on smaller screens

## Profile Header

A profile header built on `data-layout="media"`: a large avatar in the figure column, with the name, role, bio, stats row and edit button stacked beside it. Ideal for the top of a user's profile page.

The hgroup mutes the role, `data-variant="stacked"` mutes the stat labels and drops the `<dd>` indent, and `<strong>` weights the numbers. No extra CSS is needed: a stacked list that is also `data-layout` spaces its groups with the layout's gap instead of a block margin.

profile-header.html:

```html
<layout-card data-padding="xl">
  <header data-layout="media" data-layout-gap="xl">
    <!-- Avatar: slot="figure" puts it in the media column -->
    <user-avatar data-size="2xl" slot="figure">
      <span data-fallback>JD</span>
    </user-avatar>

    <!-- Name and Role -->
    <hgroup>
      <h1>Jane Doe</h1>
      <p>Senior Product Designer</p>
    </hgroup>

    <!-- Bio -->
    <p>Passionate about creating intuitive user experiences...</p>

    <!-- Stats -->
    <dl data-layout="cluster" data-layout-gap="xl" data-variant="stacked">
      <div>
        <dt>Posts</dt>
        <dd><strong>142</strong></dd>
      </div>
      <div>
        <dt>Followers</dt>
        <dd><strong>12.4K</strong></dd>
      </div>
      <div>
        <dt>Following</dt>
        <dd><strong>891</strong></dd>
      </div>
    </dl>

    <!-- Edit Button -->
    <p>
      <button type="button" class="button secondary">
        <icon-wc name="edit" size="sm"></icon-wc>
        Edit Profile
      </button>
    </p>
  </header>
</layout-card>
```

## Profile Card

A compact profile card suitable for user lists, team member displays, or search results. Features an avatar, name, email, description, and action buttons.

No custom CSS: `<hgroup>` mutes the email line, and `slot="figure"` sends the avatar to the media column.

profile-card.html:

```html
<layout-card data-padding="l">
  <layout-stack data-layout-gap="m">
    <header data-layout="media" data-layout-gap="m" data-layout-align="center">
      <user-avatar data-size="lg" slot="figure">
        <img src="user-photo.jpg" alt="Alex Thompson" />
      </user-avatar>
      <hgroup>
        <h2>Alex Thompson</h2>
        <p><a href="mailto:alex@example.com">alex@example.com</a></p>
      </hgroup>
    </header>
    <p>Full-stack developer with 8 years of experience.</p>
    <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s">
      <button type="button" class="button small">
        <icon-wc name="mail" size="sm"></icon-wc>
        Message
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="button small secondary">
        <icon-wc name="user-plus" size="sm"></icon-wc>
        Follow
      </button>
    </layout-cluster>
  </layout-stack>
</layout-card>
```

## Full Profile Page

A complete profile page layout with a sidebar containing user info and a main content area showing an `<activity-feed>`. Uses `<layout-sidebar>` with an `<aside>` for the responsive two-column layout.

`<activity-feed>` lays out each `<article data-activity>` with its icon rail and turns the authored `<time>` into a relative timestamp. The only page CSS is the stat-row rule shown under Profile Header.

profile-full.html:

```html
<layout-sidebar data-layout-gap="xl" data-layout-sidebar-width="wide" data-layout-content-min="m">
  <!-- Profile Sidebar -->
  <aside aria-label="Profile">
    <layout-card data-padding="l">
      <layout-center data-layout-intrinsic data-layout-text data-layout-gutter="none" data-layout-gap="l">
        <user-avatar data-size="2xl">
          <img src="user-photo.jpg" alt="Sarah Chen" />
          <span data-status="online"></span>
        </user-avatar>

        <hgroup data-align="center">
          <h1>Sarah Chen</h1>
          <p>Engineering Manager</p>
        </hgroup>

        <p>Leading distributed teams...</p>

        <dl data-layout="cluster" data-layout-gap="l" data-layout-justify="center" data-variant="stacked">
          <div>
            <dt>Posts</dt>
            <dd><strong>89</strong></dd>
          </div>
          <!-- More stats... -->
        </dl>

        <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s" data-layout-justify="center">
          <button type="button" class="button">Follow</button>
          <button type="button" class="button secondary">Message</button>
        </layout-cluster>
      </layout-center>
    </layout-card>
  </aside>

  <!-- Activity Feed -->
  <section data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="l" aria-labelledby="activity-heading">
    <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between">
      <h2 id="activity-heading">Recent Activity</h2>
      <!-- Filter buttons -->
    </header>

    <layout-card>
      <activity-feed aria-label="Recent activity">
        <article data-activity data-activity-icon="file-text">
          Published <a href="/posts/microservices">Building Resilient Microservices</a>
          <time datetime="2026-07-06T08:00:00Z">Jul 6, 2026</time>
        </article>
        <!-- More activity entries... -->
      </activity-feed>
    </layout-card>
  </section>
</layout-sidebar>
```

## Configuration

Profile patterns use these layout elements and attributes:

## Usage Notes

- Avatar fallbacks: Always provide initials via `<span data-fallback>` as a fallback when images fail to load
- Status indicators: Use `<span data-status="online">` inside `user-avatar` to show user presence
- Heading groups: Use `<hgroup>` for name + role pairs — the `<p>` inside automatically gets muted color styling
- Semantic stats: Use `<dl data-variant="stacked">` with one `<div>` per stat, label (`<dt>`) before value (`<dd>`), instead of generic `<div>` / `<span>` elements
- Responsive layouts: The sidebar layout automatically stacks on smaller screens when `data-layout-content-min` is reached
- Sticky sidebar: `data-layout-sticky` works on `<nav>` and `<aside>` within page layouts, not on `<layout-card>`
- Accessibility: Ensure avatar images have meaningful `alt` text and buttons have clear labels
- Stats formatting: Use abbreviated numbers (e.g., 12.4K) for large counts to maintain visual balance
- Empty states: Provide helpful messages when activity feeds are empty

## Related

Admin dashboards with stats and data tables

Avatar element documentation and API

Card container element documentation

Icon element documentation and available icons

Accessible feed of timestamped user actions

# Settings

Settings page patterns with grouped sections, sidebar navigation, and tabbed interfaces for application preferences and configuration.

- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/patterns/application/settings/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Overview

Settings patterns provide organized interfaces for managing user preferences, account configuration, and application options. These layouts scale from simple single-page forms to complex multi-section configurations.

Key features:
- Grouped sections with fieldset and legend for logical organization
- Sidebar navigation for multi-page settings with persistent nav
- Tab-based organization for compact, single-page layouts
- Toggle switches and radio groups for preference selection
- Clear save/cancel actions with form validation

## Grouped Sections

A straightforward settings layout using fieldset sections with legend headings. Each section groups related settings together, making it easy to scan and understand the form structure.

settings-sections.html:

```html
<main data-layout="center" data-layout-max="normal">
  <form action="/settings" method="POST" data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="xl">
    <hgroup>
      <h1>Settings</h1>
      <p>Manage your account settings and preferences.</p>
    </hgroup>

    <!-- Profile Section -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Profile</legend>
      <layout-stack data-layout-gap="l">
        <form-field>
          <label for="name">Full name</label>
          <input type="text" id="name" name="name" value="John Doe"/>
        </form-field>
        <form-field>
          <label for="email">Email address</label>
          <input type="email" id="email" name="email" value="john@example.com"/>
        </form-field>
        <form-field>
          <label for="bio">Bio</label>
          <textarea id="bio" name="bio" rows="4"></textarea>
        </form-field>
      </layout-stack>
    </fieldset>

    <!-- Notifications Section -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Notifications</legend>
      <layout-stack data-layout-gap="m">
        <label>
          <input type="checkbox" name="notify_comments" checked/>
          <span>
            Comments<br/>
            <small>Get notified when someone comments on your posts.</small>
          </span>
        </label>
        <label>
          <input type="checkbox" name="notify_mentions" checked/>
          <span>
            Mentions<br/>
            <small>Get notified when someone mentions you.</small>
          </span>
        </label>
      </layout-stack>
    </fieldset>

    <!-- Privacy Section -->
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Privacy</legend>
      <layout-stack data-layout-gap="m">
        <label>
          <input type="radio" name="visibility" value="public"/>
          <span>
            Public<br/>
            <small>Anyone can view your profile and activity.</small>
          </span>
        </label>
        <label>
          <input type="radio" name="visibility" value="private" checked/>
          <span>
            Private<br/>
            <small>Only approved followers can see your activity.</small>
          </span>
        </label>
      </layout-stack>
    </fieldset>

    <footer data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="end" data-layout-gap="m">
      <button type="button" class="secondary">Cancel</button>
      <button type="submit">Save changes</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</main>
```

Fieldset styling:

```css
fieldset {
  background: var(--color-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
  border-radius: var(--radius-l);
  padding: var(--size-l);
}

fieldset legend {
  font-size: var(--font-size-l);
  font-weight: var(--font-weight-semibold);
  padding: 0 var(--size-xs);
}
```

## Sidebar Navigation

A settings layout with persistent sidebar navigation for applications with many configuration sections. The sidebar provides quick access to different settings categories while the main area displays the selected section.

`nav.vertical` stacks the links and marks the `aria-current` page. A `<layout-card>` with a `<header>` child draws each section with a divided title bar. The page adds a surface to the sidebar region and lines up each icon with its label, selecting by element:

settings-sidebar.html:

```html
<body data-page-layout="sidebar-left" data-layout-gap="none" data-layout-sidebar-width="narrow">
  <!-- Settings Navigation -->
  <nav class="vertical" aria-label="Settings navigation">
    <ul>
      <li>
        <a href="#" aria-current="page">
          <icon-wc name="cog"></icon-wc>
          General
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="#">
          <icon-wc name="shield-check"></icon-wc>
          Security
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="#">
          <icon-wc name="bell"></icon-wc>
          Notifications
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="#">
          <icon-wc name="credit-card"></icon-wc>
          Billing
        </a>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </nav>

  <!-- Settings Content -->
  <main data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="xl">
    <hgroup>
      <h1>General Settings</h1>
      <p>Manage your account preferences.</p>
    </hgroup>

    <layout-card data-padding="l">
      <header>
        <hgroup>
          <h2>Account Information</h2>
          <p>Update your personal details and contact information.</p>
        </hgroup>
      </header>
      <form data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="l">
        <!-- Form fields -->
        <button type="submit">Save changes</button>
      </form>
    </layout-card>
  </main>
</body>
```

Settings sidebar CSS:

```css
body > nav {
  background: var(--color-surface);
  border-inline-end: var(--border-width-thin) solid var(--color-border);
  padding: var(--size-l) var(--size-s);
}

body > nav a {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--size-s);
  border-radius: var(--radius-m);
}

body > main {
  padding: var(--size-xl);
}
```

## Tab Navigation

A compact settings layout using `<tab-set>` for section navigation. Each tab is a native `<details name>`, so without JavaScript the sections still open as an accordion. This pattern works well when settings fit on a single page and users need to switch between a few main categories quickly. Toggle switches use VB's built-in `<input data-switch>` for on/off settings.

`<tab-set>` draws the tab bar and panels, links each summary to its panel and handles arrow-key navigation, so the recipe needs no tab CSS or script. The demo adds one rule so setting-row headings read as labels rather than page headings:

Use VB's built-in `<input type="checkbox" data-switch>` for toggle settings — no custom CSS needed. Size variants are available with `data-switch="s"` and `data-switch="l"`.

settings-tabs.html:

```html
<layout-card>
  <tab-set aria-label="Settings sections">
    <details name="settings-tabs" open>
      <summary>Account</summary>
      <form data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="l">
        <!-- Account settings form -->
        <button type="submit">Save changes</button>
      </form>
    </details>

    <details name="settings-tabs">
      <summary>Security</summary>
      <layout-stack data-layout-gap="l">
        <layout-cluster data-layout-justify="between" data-layout-gap="l">
          <hgroup class="tight">
            <h2 id="two-factor-label">Two-factor authentication</h2>
            <p>Add an extra layer of security to your account.</p>
          </hgroup>
          <input type="checkbox" data-switch name="two_factor" aria-labelledby="two-factor-label"/>
        </layout-cluster>
        <!-- More setting rows... -->
      </layout-stack>
    </details>

    <details name="settings-tabs">
      <summary>Notifications</summary>
      <!-- Notification settings -->
    </details>

    <details name="settings-tabs">
      <summary>Billing</summary>
      <!-- Billing settings -->
    </details>
  </tab-set>
</layout-card>
```

Setting row CSS:

```css
tab-set hgroup > h2 {
  font-size: var(--font-size-m);
}
```

Toggle switch usage:

```html
<!-- Default toggle -->
<input type="checkbox" data-switch name="email_notifications"
       aria-labelledby="email-notifications-label"/>

<!-- Small toggle -->
<input type="checkbox" data-switch="s" name="compact_toggle"/>

<!-- Large toggle -->
<input type="checkbox" data-switch="l" name="prominent_toggle"/>
```

## Configuration

Settings patterns use these layout elements and attributes:

`<tab-set>` keeps the native `<details>`/`<summary>` semantics (each summary is a button) rather than applying ARIA tab roles. When it upgrades it gives the host `role="group"`, links each summary and panel with `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby`, and keeps `aria-expanded` in sync. Author only the `aria-label` on the `<tab-set>` and a shared `name` on its `<details>`.

## Usage Notes

- Toggle switches: Use `<input type="checkbox" data-switch>` for on/off settings — VB provides complete toggle styling with size variants (`data-switch="s"`, `data-switch="l"`)
- Setting rows: Use `<hgroup class="tight">` for heading + description pairs in setting rows — provides automatic muted text and margin resets
- Form validation: Show validation errors inline near the relevant field, not at the top of the page
- Save states: Provide clear feedback when settings are saved; consider auto-save for simple toggles
- Section organization: Group settings logically by category; put most-used settings first
- Keyboard navigation: `<tab-set>` provides arrow-key navigation between tabs and Enter/Space to activate
- Loading states: Show skeleton placeholders while loading settings to prevent layout shift
- Confirmation dialogs: Confirm before destructive actions like account deletion or password changes
- Deep linking: Support URL fragments or query params to link directly to specific settings sections
- Mobile considerations: Convert sidebar nav to a dropdown or stacked layout on small screens

Admin dashboards with stats and data tables

Application shell layouts with navigation

Multi-step form workflows

Form input wrapper with labels and validation

SVG icon component with Lucide icons

# App Shells

Application shell layouts for web apps, dashboards, and admin interfaces. Header, sidebar, and content area patterns.

- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/patterns/application/shells/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Overview

App shells define the overall structure of your application, organizing navigation, content areas, and auxiliary panels. Choose a layout based on your application's navigation needs and content complexity.

Key features:
- Semantic HTML5 structure with header, nav, main, and aside
- Responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes
- Flexible content areas using layout primitives
- Accessible navigation patterns with proper ARIA labels

## Stacked Layout

The traditional layout with a header on top and main content below. Best for content-focused applications where vertical space is important.

A button holding only an `<icon-wc>` plus an `aria-label` is squared automatically; no extra class is needed.

shell-stacked.html:

```html
<body data-page-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="none">
  <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between">
    <a href="/"><brand-mark>AppName</brand-mark></a>
    <nav class="horizontal pills" aria-label="Main navigation">
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/dashboard" aria-current="page">Dashboard</a></li>
        <li><a href="/projects">Projects</a></li>
        <li><a href="/reports">Reports</a></li>
        <li><a href="/settings">Settings</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
    <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s">
      <button type="button" class="button small" aria-label="Notifications">
        <icon-wc name="bell"></icon-wc>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="button small" aria-label="User menu">
        <icon-wc name="user"></icon-wc>
      </button>
    </layout-cluster>
  </header>

  <main>
    <layout-center data-layout-max="wide" data-layout-gap="l">
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <!-- Page content here -->
    </layout-center>
  </main>

  <footer>
    <p>&copy; 2026 AppName. All rights reserved.</p>
  </footer>
</body>
```

## Sidebar + Content

A fixed sidebar navigation with a main content area. Ideal for dashboards and admin interfaces with many navigation items.

shell-sidebar.html:

```html
<body data-page-layout="sidebar-left" data-layout-gap="none" data-layout-sidebar-width="narrow">
  <nav class="vertical" data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="l" data-layout-sticky aria-label="Main navigation">
    <a href="/"><brand-mark>AppName</brand-mark></a>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="/dashboard" aria-current="page">
        <icon-wc name="home"></icon-wc> Dashboard
      </a></li>
      <li><a href="/projects">
        <icon-wc name="folder"></icon-wc> Projects
      </a></li>
      <li><a href="/team">
        <icon-wc name="users"></icon-wc> Team
      </a></li>
      <li><a href="/reports">
        <icon-wc name="chart-bar"></icon-wc> Reports
      </a></li>
      <li><a href="/settings">
        <icon-wc name="cog"></icon-wc> Settings
      </a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>

  <main data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="none">
    <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between">
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <layout-cluster data-layout-gap="s">
        <input type="search" placeholder="Search..." aria-label="Search" />
        <button type="button" class="button" aria-label="User menu">
          <icon-wc name="user"></icon-wc>
        </button>
      </layout-cluster>
    </header>

    <section data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="l">
      <!-- Page content here -->
    </section>
  </main>
</body>
```

## Multi-Column Layout

A three-column layout with sidebar navigation, main content, and a right panel. Perfect for email clients, chat applications, or content management systems.

The message list is this recipe's own look. It needs no classes: the rules select the list by position and the selected message by `aria-current`.

shell-multi-column.html:

```html
<body data-page-layout="holy-grail" data-layout-gap="none" data-layout-sidebar-width="narrow">
  <nav class="vertical" data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="m" data-layout-sticky aria-label="Mail folders">
    <a href="/"><brand-mark data-size="l">Mail</brand-mark></a>
    <button type="button" class="button">Compose</button>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="/inbox" aria-current="page">
        <icon-wc name="inbox"></icon-wc> Inbox <layout-badge>12</layout-badge>
      </a></li>
      <li><a href="/sent"><icon-wc name="send"></icon-wc> Sent</a></li>
      <li><a href="/drafts"><icon-wc name="file-text"></icon-wc> Drafts</a></li>
      <li><a href="/trash"><icon-wc name="trash"></icon-wc> Trash</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>

  <main data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="none">
    <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between">
      <h1>Inbox</h1>
      <input type="search" placeholder="Search mail..." aria-label="Search mail" />
    </header>
    <ul>
      <li aria-current="true">
        <time>10:32 AM</time>
        <strong>Alice Johnson</strong>
        <p>Project Update: Q1 Goals</p>
        <p>Hi team, I wanted to share a quick update...</p>
      </li>
      <!-- More messages -->
    </ul>
  </main>

  <aside data-layout-sticky>
    <header>
      <h2>Project Update: Q1 Goals</h2>
      <!-- Sender and time -->
    </header>
    <!-- Selected message body -->
    <footer data-layout="cluster" data-layout-gap="s">
      <button type="button" class="button">Reply</button>
    </footer>
  </aside>
</body>
```

Message list CSS:

```css
main > ul {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
main > ul > li {
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--size-m) var(--size-l);
  border-block-end: 1px solid var(--color-border);
  background: var(--color-surface);
}
main > ul > li[aria-current] {
  background: var(--color-primary-subtle);
  border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--color-primary);
}
main > ul > li > :is(strong, p) {
  display: block;
  margin: 0 0 var(--size-2xs);
}
main > ul > li > p:last-child {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--font-size-s);
  color: var(--color-text-muted);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
main > ul > li > time {
  font-size: var(--font-size-xs);
  color: var(--color-text-muted);
  float: inline-end;
}
```

## Collapsible Sidebar

A sidebar that can collapse to icons only, using native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements. Great for maximizing content space while keeping navigation accessible.

`.logo` and `.nav-label` are this recipe's own hooks, not VB classes. The logo stays a plain block link instead of `<brand-mark>` because the collapsed rail shows only its `::first-letter`, which needs a block container (brand-mark is inline-flex). `.nav-label` marks the text the rail hides. The rest selects by element and the `open` state of the `<details>`:

shell-collapsible.html:

```html
<body data-page-layout="sidebar-left" data-layout-gap="none" data-layout-sidebar-width="narrow">
  <nav aria-label="Main navigation">
    <details open>
      <summary>
        <icon-wc name="menu"></icon-wc>
        <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle sidebar</span>
      </summary>
      <layout-stack data-layout-gap="l">
        <a href="#" class="logo">AppName</a>
        <nav class="vertical" aria-label="Sidebar links">
          <ul>
            <li><a href="/dashboard" aria-current="page">
              <icon-wc name="home"></icon-wc>
              <span class="nav-label">Dashboard</span>
            </a></li>
            <!-- more nav items -->
          </ul>
        </nav>
      </layout-stack>
    </details>
  </nav>

  <main data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="none">
    <header data-layout="cluster" data-layout-justify="between">
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <!-- Header actions -->
    </header>
    <section data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="xl" aria-label="Overview">
      <!-- Page content here -->
    </section>
  </main>
</body>
```

Collapsible sidebar CSS:

```css
body > nav > details {
  height: 100%;
  background: var(--color-surface);
  border-inline-end: 1px solid var(--color-border);
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}
body > nav > details > layout-stack {
  padding: var(--size-m);
  flex: 1;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
.logo {
  display: block;
  font-weight: 600;
  font-size: var(--font-size-l);
  text-decoration: none;
  color: var(--color-text);
}

/* Collapsed: narrow the page-layout sidebar, show icons only */
body:has(> nav > details:not([open])) {
  --_sidebar-width: 4rem;
}
details:not([open]) .logo {
  font-size: 0;
}
details:not([open]) .logo::first-letter {
  font-size: var(--font-size-l);
}
details:not([open]) .nav-label {
  display: none;
}
details:not([open]) nav.vertical a {
  padding: var(--size-s);
  justify-content: center;
}

/* Expanded: icon and label side by side */
details[open] nav.vertical a {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--size-s);
}
```

## Configuration

App shells use these layout elements and attributes:

## Usage Notes

- Full height: `data-page-layout` handles this automatically with `min-height: 100dvh`
- Sticky elements: Use the `data-layout-sticky` attribute on nav or aside elements
- Responsive: `data-page-layout` layouts auto-stack on narrow viewports (< 768px)
- Collapsible sidebar: Use `<details>`/`<summary>` inside `<nav>` for zero-JS collapse
- Accessibility: Include skip links, proper heading hierarchy, and ARIA labels on navigation landmarks
