# <include-file>

Fetch a same-origin HTML fragment, sanitize it, and insert it into the page

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/include-file/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<include-file src="/partials/header.html">
  <p><a href="/">Home</a></p>
</include-file>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | string |  | URL of the HTML fragment, resolved against the page (document.baseURI). Only same-origin http(s) URLs load; blob:, data:, javascript: and other schemes are always refused; other origins need allow-cross-origin. A same-origin URL that redirects off-origin is refused. Observed: changing it re-fetches (honouring lazy); a change made while detached loads on reconnect. |
| `mode` | `replace`, `append`, `prepend` | `replace` | How fetched content is inserted. append/prepend leave existing children (including author scripts) untouched. Unknown values behave as replace and log a warning. |
| `lazy` | boolean |  | Defer loading until the element is within 200px of the viewport (also for later src changes) |
| `trusted` | boolean |  | Author vouches for the source: insert the fetched HTML without sanitizing. Without it the fragment goes through VB's sanitizer (no scripts, on* handlers, javascript: URLs, iframes, forms…). Never set it for URLs that serve user-generated content. |
| `allow-scripts` | boolean |  | Run the fragment's scripts (each once per load). Requires trusted; ignored with a console warning otherwise. |
| `allow-cross-origin` | boolean |  | Permit fetching from another origin (the server must allow it via CORS). Content is still sanitized unless trusted is also set. |
| `data-label-error` | string | `Failed to load content` | Text of the role="alert" error message shown when a load fails and no fallback content remains |
| `data-loading` | boolean |  | Present while content is loading (aria-busy="true" is set alongside) |
| `data-loaded` | boolean |  | Present after successful load |
| `data-error` | boolean |  | Present if the fetch fails or the URL is refused (origin, scheme, include cycle, nesting deeper than 10) |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include-file:loaded` | `{ src, url, html }` | After the fragment is inserted. src is the attribute value, url the resolved absolute URL, html the markup as inserted (sanitized unless trusted). |
| `include-file:error` | `{ src, error }` | When the fetch fails or the load is refused; error is a message string. The original fallback is restored on a first-load failure in replace mode. |
| `include-file:src-changed` | `{ src, source: 'property' }` | After .src is assigned a new value from script (not for direct attribute changes) |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `reload()` | Re-fetch the current src (same policy checks as a normal load). |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | Mirror of the src attribute. Setting it updates the attribute (which loads the new URL) and fires include-file:src-changed. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Live region
- The component manages: `aria-busy`, `role="alert"`

---

# <layout-badge>

Small inline status or count badge. Colour reinforces the text, never replaces it. Surface elements use bare data-* attributes.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/layout-badge/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-badge>Default</layout-badge>
<layout-badge data-color="primary">Primary</layout-badge>
<layout-badge data-color="success">Success</layout-badge>
<layout-badge data-color="warning">Warning</layout-badge>
<layout-badge data-color="error">Error</layout-badge>
<layout-badge data-color="info">Info</layout-badge>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-size` | `s`, `l` |  | Size: s (11px floor) or l; omit for the default (--font-size-xs). |
| `data-color` | `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `brand`, `secondary`, `accent` |  | Semantic (primary, success, warning, error, info) or theme (brand, secondary, accent) colour. Colour is never the only signal: the badge text must carry the meaning. |
| `data-variant` | `subtle`, `outlined` |  | subtle (mode-aware tint with --color-*-text ink) or outlined (transparent, border in the text colour) instead of filled. |
| `data-shape` | `square`, `ribbon`, `notch`, `flag`, `double-arrow`, `stamp` |  | square: square corners instead of a pill. ribbon (V cut at the inline end), notch (V cut at the inline start), flag (point at the inline end), double-arrow (points at both ends) and stamp (concave corners) are decorative shapes painted behind the text; they mirror in RTL, never clip the label or the focus outline, and fall back to a bordered rectangle in forced colours. Tune the notch depth with --badge-notch. |

## CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--badge-notch` | Notch / point depth of the decorative data-shape values (default 0.75em); the padding on the notched side grows by the same length. |
| `--badge-shape-fill` | Fill of a decorative shape (default: the badge background for its data-color / data-variant). Accepts gradients. |

---

# <layout-canvas>

Elevated content surface (a panel with radius, shadow and a 1px edge: a hairline on a plain page, transparent under data-backdrop, CanvasText in forced colours). Attribute form: data-canvas on a semantic element (not data-layout), with the variant as its value: data-canvas (default), data-canvas="flush" or data-canvas="elevated". Below 37.5rem every canvas goes flush with reduced inline padding unless data-padding is set. Surface elements use bare data-* attributes.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/layout-canvas/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<!-- Attribute form (preferred) -->
<article data-canvas>
  <h2>Article with a canvas surface</h2>
  <p>The article itself is the surface: no wrapper element.</p>
</article>

<!-- Element form -->
<layout-canvas>
  <h2>Layout canvas element</h2>
  <p>The same surface as a wrapper.</p>
</layout-canvas>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-canvas` | (no value), `flush`, `elevated` |  | Attribute form: makes any element a canvas; the value is the variant (bare = default, flush, elevated). Use data-variant on the <layout-canvas> element instead. |
| `data-variant` | `flush`, `elevated` |  | Element form only: flush (no radius or shadow) or elevated (larger radius and shadow, 37.5rem and up). The attribute form puts the variant in data-canvas itself. |
| `data-max` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide`, `prose` |  | Max inline size, centered: narrow / normal / wide (--content-* tokens) or prose (65ch). |
| `data-padding` | `none`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | `l` | Padding on all sides. An explicit value is kept below 37.5rem (otherwise the inline padding drops to --size-m there). |
| `data-canvas-depth` | `1`, `2` |  | Stacked-paper effect with 1 or 2 sheets behind the surface (37.5rem and wider; not on flush). |

---

# <layout-card>

Card surface. Element only: there is no data-layout or data-card attribute form; for a surface on a semantic element use data-canvas, for collections use <card-list>. A plain padded block by default; a header / section / footer child (or slot="header|content|footer") switches it to structured mode: header pinned on top, footer pinned at the bottom, every other child stacked between in source order. Surface elements use bare data-* attributes.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/layout-card/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-card>
  Default card with subtle shadow
</layout-card>

<layout-card data-variant="elevated">
  Elevated card with stronger shadow
</layout-card>

<layout-card data-variant="outlined">
  Outlined card with border
</layout-card>

<layout-card data-variant="ghost">
  Ghost card with no background
</layout-card>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-variant` | `elevated`, `outlined`, `ghost` |  | Visual style: elevated (shadow), outlined (border), ghost (no surface). |
| `data-padding` | `none`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | `m` | Internal padding. Block mode pads the card by the token (none/s/m/l/xl). Structured mode pads the children one step up: header/footer --size-m/--size-l and content --size-l at the default m (s: xs/s and s; l: l/xl and xl; xl: xl/2xl and 2xl); none also drops the header/footer dividers. |
| `data-max` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide`, `prose` |  | Max inline size, centered (margin-inline: auto in block flow, align-self in flex/grid): --content-narrow / --content-normal / --content-wide, or prose (65ch). Same keyword set as layout-center and canvas. |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `header` | Structured mode: pinned to the top, padded, with a bottom divider. A direct h1-h6 inside loses its margin and uses --font-size-l. |
| `section` | Structured mode: a content child. Every child that is not the header or footer is content and stacks in source order, one body padding apart. |
| `footer` | Structured mode: pinned to the bottom (margin-block-start: auto), top divider, wrapping flex row of actions aligned to the inline end. |
| `[slot="header"]` | Any element treated as the header (also triggers structured mode). |
| `[slot="content"]` | Any element treated as content (also triggers structured mode, so a slot-only card works). |
| `[slot="footer"]` | Any element treated as the footer (also triggers structured mode). |

---

# <layout-center>

Horizontally centered, max-width-constrained container with side gutters. Attribute form: data-layout="center".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/center/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-center data-layout-max="narrow" data-layout-text>
  <article>
    <h3>Release notes</h3>
    <p>Capped at 40rem and centred.</p>
  </article>
</layout-center>

<article data-layout="center" data-layout-max="narrow" data-layout-text>
  <h3>Release notes</h3>
  <p>Capped at 40rem and centred.</p>
</article>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-max` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide`, `prose` | `normal` | Max inline size of the content box (box-sizing: content-box; the gutter is added outside): narrow (--content-narrow, 40rem), normal (--content-normal, 60rem), wide (--content-wide, 80rem) or prose (65ch). |
| `data-layout-intrinsic` | boolean |  | Center narrower-than-max content intrinsically (flex column, align center). |
| `data-layout-text` | boolean |  | Center the text as well. |
| `data-layout-gutter` | `none`, `s`, `l` | `m` | Inline padding on each side: none, s or l. The default --size-m applies when the attribute is omitted; there is no m value. The box is content-box, so the gutter adds to the max width. |
| `data-layout-gap` | (no value), `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Become a full-width flex column (inline-size fills the parent minus the gutters) with this gap between children, on the shared size scale. Bare attribute = m. |

---

# <layout-cluster>

Horizontal wrapping flex row for groups of short items — tags, buttons, metadata. Attribute form: data-layout="cluster".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/cluster/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-cluster data-layout-gap="xs">
  <layout-badge>HTML</layout-badge>
  <layout-badge>CSS</layout-badge>
  <layout-badge>JavaScript</layout-badge>
</layout-cluster>

<ul class="unstyled" data-layout="cluster" data-layout-gap="xs">
  <li><layout-badge>HTML</layout-badge></li>
  <li><layout-badge>CSS</layout-badge></li>
  <li><layout-badge>JavaScript</layout-badge></li>
</ul>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `s` | Gap between items, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-justify` | `start`, `end`, `center`, `between` | `start` | Main-axis distribution. |
| `data-layout-align` | `start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch`, `baseline` | `center` | Cross-axis alignment. |
| `data-layout-nowrap` | boolean |  | Keep everything on one line; no wrapping. Items overflow a narrow container, so let it scroll (overflow-x: auto). |
| `data-layout-overlap` | (no value), `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l` | `s` | Overlap items (avatar groups) in DOM order, later items on top, each with a surface-coloured ring. Items after the first are pulled back by xs 0.25rem, s 0.5rem, m 0.75rem or l 1rem. Forces gap 0. Bare attribute = s. Use a ul with one li per avatar, aria-labelledby on the list and an aria-label on the "+N" chip. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-container` | main, article, section, aside | boolean |  | Opt a semantic child back into container queries. The layout removes container-type from such children so they size to content; this restores it. |

---

# <layout-columns>

Multi-column text flow with a readable measure, vertical rhythm (between direct children), column rules and break hygiene. Attribute form: data-layout="columns" (same modifiers), usually on an <article data-prose>. <reader-view> needs the element form.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/layout-columns/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-columns data-layout-column-count="2">
  <h2>The Measure</h2>
  <p>…</p>
  <p>…</p>
</layout-columns>

<!-- Same layout, no wrapper element -->
<article data-layout="columns" data-layout-column-count="2" data-prose>
  <h2>The Measure</h2>
  <p>…</p>
  <p>…</p>
</article>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-align` | `justify` |  | justify: justified text with automatic hyphenation. Justified narrow columns form uneven word gaps (WCAG 1.4.8, AAA): prefer ragged-right for long text. |
| `data-layout-column-count` | `1`, `2`, `3`, `auto` | `1` | Number of columns. 2 and 3 are maximums: below about 14rem per column they drop to fewer columns (one on a phone). auto fits as many --column-min-width (38ch) columns as the element's own width allows. |
| `data-layout-measure` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide` | `normal` | Line measure (--measure-narrow / --measure-normal / --measure-wide). Count 1 caps the block width. Counts 2 and 3 cap each column, so the block is at most count × measure + gaps (without the attribute they fill the container). auto uses the measure as the column width. |
| `data-layout-max` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide` | `normal` | Same as data-layout-measure (ch-based, unlike layout-center's rem-based data-layout-max). |
| `data-layout-centered` | boolean |  | No effect: columns are always centered (margin-inline: auto). Read by the shared typographic core. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-bleed` | direct child | boolean |  | Break out to the full inline size of the nearest query container (main, article, section). Spans every column in a multi-column flow. |

---

# <layout-cover>

Full-height (min-block-size) flex column that vertically centers a principal element (data-layout-principal; a sole child auto-centers), with header/footer or cover-top/-bottom children pinned to the edges. Attribute form: data-layout="cover".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/cover/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-cover data-layout-centered style="--layout-min: 14rem">
  <header><small>Header</small></header>
  <hgroup data-layout-principal>
    <h3>Launching soon</h3>
    <p>The principal is centred vertically.</p>
  </hgroup>
  <footer><small>Footer</small></footer>
</layout-cover>

<section data-layout="cover" data-layout-centered aria-label="Launch" style="--layout-min: 14rem">
  <header><small>Header</small></header>
  <hgroup data-layout-principal>
    <h3>Launching soon</h3>
    <p>The principal is centred vertically.</p>
  </hgroup>
  <footer><small>Footer</small></footer>
</section>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-min` | `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `auto` | `xl` | Minimum block size: 50 / 70 / 80vh, xl = 100dvh, auto = none. One-off: style="--layout-min: 65vh" (beats the token; registered inherits:false so it never reaches nested layouts; layout-grid reads the same property as its minimum column width). |
| `data-layout-padding` | `none`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | `m` | Padding on all sides. |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `none` | Minimum space between all children (top, principal, bottom), on the shared size scale. The principal's auto margins still centre it. |
| `data-layout-centered` | boolean |  | Center the principal and text horizontally; header/footer (and data-layout-cover-top/-bottom) children still span the full width. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-principal` | any child | boolean |  | The vertically centered principal element. A sole child auto-centers without it. |
| `data-layout-cover-top` | any child | boolean |  | Pin to the top (a <header> child is pinned automatically). |
| `data-layout-cover-bottom` | any child | boolean |  | Pin to the bottom (a <footer> child is pinned automatically). |
| `data-container` | main, article, section, aside | boolean |  | With data-layout-centered, the layout removes container-type from semantic children so they size to their content instead of collapsing; this opts one back into container queries. |

---

# <layout-grid>

Auto-fit responsive grid: as many columns as fit the minimum width, then wrap. Attribute form: data-layout="grid".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/grid/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-grid data-layout-min="s" data-layout-gap="s">
  <layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Alpha</p></layout-card>
  <layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Beta</p></layout-card>
  <layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Gamma</p></layout-card>
</layout-grid>

<ul class="unstyled" data-layout="grid" data-layout-min="s" data-layout-gap="s">
  <li><layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Alpha</p></layout-card></li>
  <li><layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Beta</p></layout-card></li>
  <li><layout-card data-variant="outlined" data-padding="s"><p>Gamma</p></layout-card></li>
</ul>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-min` | `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | `m` | Minimum column width before wrapping: 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25rem. Tracks are clamped to the container (min(…, 100%)), so a grid narrower than the minimum shows one full-width column instead of overflowing. One-off lengths: style="--layout-min: 220px" (not inherited by nested grids). |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Gap between cells, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-subgrid` | (no value), `2`, `3`, `4` | `3` | Each child becomes a subgrid spanning 2, 3 or 4 rows (bare = 3; any other value also spans 3) so header/content/footer line up across siblings. The subgridded rows use the grid's row gap, so data-layout-gap also spaces the parts inside each child — set row-gap on the children to override. Any child works, including article/section (they are not query containers here unless they carry data-container, which opts them out of subgrid alignment). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-container` | main, article, section, aside | boolean |  | Opt a semantic child of a data-layout-subgrid grid back into container queries. The layout removes container-type from such children so they can be subgrids; this restores it, and the child then sizes its own rows. |

---

# <layout-imposter>

Positioned overlay centred over (or pinned to an edge or corner of) its containing block, logically (mirrored in RTL). Element only: there is no data-layout form. Prerequisite: the element it sits over needs position: relative (any non-static position); data-layout-fixed positions against the viewport instead. Visual positioning only: no focus trap, inert background or dialog semantics; use <dialog> or [popover] for modal UI. Stacking order: --imposter-z (default 1, --z-float when fixed).

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/imposter/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<section class="stage">
  <layout-imposter>
    <layout-card>Centered content</layout-card>
  </layout-imposter>
</section>

<style>
  .stage { position: relative; block-size: 200px; }
</style>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-fixed` | boolean |  | Position relative to the viewport instead of the containing block. |
| `data-layout-margin` | `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` |  | Inset from the edges when pinned to one (and the contain inset). |
| `data-layout-position` | `center`, `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`, `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end` | `center` | Where to place the overlay. |
| `data-layout-contain` | boolean |  | Never larger than the containing block (the positioned ancestor, or the viewport when fixed) minus the margin on each side; scrolls inside when the content is bigger. |

---

# <layout-reel>

Horizontal scrolling strip with proximity snap points, an optional scrollbar and edge hints. Attribute form: data-layout="reel" (same modifiers). When the items hold no focusable content, name the reel and make it focusable: <section data-layout="reel" aria-label="…" tabindex="0">, or <layout-reel role="region" aria-label="…" tabindex="0">.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/reel/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<!-- Element form: add the region role yourself -->
<layout-reel data-layout-item-width="s" role="region" aria-label="Featured items" tabindex="0">
  <layout-card>...</layout-card>
  <layout-card>...</layout-card>
</layout-reel>

<!-- Attribute form: a named section is already a region landmark -->
<section data-layout="reel" data-layout-item-width="s" aria-label="Featured items" tabindex="0">
  <layout-card>...</layout-card>
  <layout-card>...</layout-card>
</section>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-scrollbar` | boolean |  | Show a thin scrollbar. Hidden by default, except under forced colours and on touch-only (hover: none) devices, where it always shows. |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Gap between items, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-padding` | `none`, `s`, `m`, `l` | `s` | Padding on all sides (block padding leaves room for focus rings and shadows); the same value is the inline scroll padding. |
| `data-layout-item-width` | `auto`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `full` | `auto` | Item width: auto (content), s / m / l / xl tokens, or full (100%). |
| `data-layout-align` | `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` | `stretch` | Cross-axis alignment of items. |
| `data-scroll-hint` | (no value), `start` |  | Fade the edges to hint at overflow, logically (mirrored in RTL). Where scroll-driven animations are supported each edge fades only while there is more content that way; elsewhere both edges fade. start: only the end edge ever fades. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-container` | main, article, section, aside | boolean |  | Opt a semantic child back into container queries (the reel removes container-type from such children so they size to content). |

---

# <layout-sidebar>

Two-column layout: a fixed-basis sidebar beside a flexible content column that wraps below it when there is no room. nav and aside children are the sidebar; every other child is content (hr, [role=separator], template, script and style are skipped); without nav/aside the first child is the sidebar and the last the content. Attribute form: data-layout="sidebar".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/sidebar/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-sidebar data-layout-gap="m">
  <nav aria-label="Sections">...</nav>
  <article>...</article>
</layout-sidebar>

<section data-layout="sidebar" data-layout-gap="m" aria-label="Settings">
  <nav aria-label="Sections">...</nav>
  <article>...</article>
</section>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Gap between the columns, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-side` | `end` |  | end: put the sidebar on the end side. Omit the attribute for the start side (there is no start value). nav/aside children keep DOM order (order: 1); the positional fallback reverses the row (flex-direction: row-reverse), so visual order then differs from DOM order. |
| `data-layout-sidebar-width` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide` | `normal` | Sidebar basis: 12 / 16 / 20rem (the same three values in every sidebar context). |
| `data-layout-content-min` | `s`, `m`, `l` | `m` | Content column floor before wrapping: 40 / 50 / 60%. One-off: style="--layout-content-min: 45%". |
| `data-layout-nowrap` | boolean |  | Never wrap; the sidebar stays beside the content, also inside a narrow (< 40rem) data-page-layout main. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-sticky` | nav, aside | boolean |  | Sticky sidebar with its own scroll, active when the page opts into the smart sticky system (:root[data-sticky]). |

---

# <layout-stack>

Vertical flex stack with a consistent gap between children. Attribute form: any semantic element with data-layout="stack". With data-layout-align start/center/end, main/article/section/aside children drop container-type so they size to content instead of collapsing to zero width; add data-container to such a child to keep its container queries.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/stack/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<form action="/search" method="get">
  <layout-stack data-layout-gap="s">
    <label for="q">Search</label>
    <input type="search" id="q" name="q" />
    <button type="submit">Go</button>
  </layout-stack>
</form>

<form data-layout="stack" data-layout-gap="s" action="/search" method="get">
  <label for="q2">Search</label>
  <input type="search" id="q2" name="q" />
  <button type="submit">Go</button>
</form>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Gap between children, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-align` | `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` | `stretch` | Cross-axis (inline) alignment of children. start/center/end make children content-sized (semantic sectioning children stop being query containers — see data-container). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-container` | main, article, section, aside | boolean |  | Opt a semantic child back into container queries when the stack is aligned start/center/end. The layout removes container-type from such children so they size to content; this restores it (give the child an explicit inline size, or it collapses). |

---

# <layout-switcher>

Flex row that switches to a column once the switcher's own width drops below the threshold (a flex-basis formula, no media or container query). Attribute form: data-layout="switcher" (same modifiers).

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/switcher/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-switcher data-layout-gap="s" data-layout-threshold="l">
  <article>One</article>
  <article>Two</article>
</layout-switcher>

<section data-layout="switcher" data-layout-gap="s" data-layout-threshold="l">
  <article>One</article>
  <article>Two</article>
</section>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-gap` | `none`, `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`, `3xl` | `m` | Gap between items, on the shared size scale. |
| `data-layout-threshold` | `s`, `m`, `l` | `m` | The switcher's own width below which the row becomes a column: 25 / 30 / 40rem. No container query is involved. One-off: style="--layout-threshold: 35rem" (not inherited by nested switchers). |
| `data-layout-limit` | `2`, `3`, `4` |  | Force the column layout once there are more than this many items. |
| `data-layout-reverse` | boolean |  | Reverse the visual order when stacked (flex-wrap: wrap-reverse): the last item is on top once items wrap onto their own lines; the row keeps DOM order. Visual only — focus and reading order stay in DOM order, so use it only when the stacked order is presentational. |

---

# <layout-text>

Long-form reading container: a readable measure plus vertical rhythm between direct children. Attribute form: data-layout="prose" (there is no data-layout="text"). article[data-measure] gives the measure (centered) without the rhythm. Owns the typographic core shared with layout-columns and data-layout="columns".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/layout-text/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<layout-text data-layout-measure="narrow">
  <h2>Reading Width</h2>
  <p>Measure and vertical rhythm on a wrapper element.</p>
</layout-text>

<article data-layout="prose" data-layout-max="narrow">
  <h2>Reading Width</h2>
  <p>The same measure and rhythm on the article itself.</p>
</article>

<article data-measure="narrow">
  <h2>Reading Width</h2>
  <p>Capped and centered, browser-default spacing.</p>
</article>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-layout-measure` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide` | `normal` | Line measure: --measure-narrow / --measure-normal / --measure-wide (45 / 65 / 80ch by default; data-fluid and the accessibility themes adjust the tokens). Released to 100% in containers narrower than 30rem. |
| `data-layout-max` | `narrow`, `normal`, `wide` | `normal` | Same as data-layout-measure (the prose attribute form spells it this way). ch-based — layout-center's data-layout-max="narrow" is 40rem, this one is 45ch. |
| `data-layout-centered` | boolean |  | Center the container (margin-inline: auto). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-bleed` | direct child | boolean |  | Break out to the full inline size of the nearest query container (main, article, section). Works centered or not; centered text bleeds symmetrically. |

---

# <loading-spinner>

CSS-only animated loading spinner. Standalone: add role="status" + aria-label. Next to visible text: add aria-hidden="true".

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/loading-spinner/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<loading-spinner role="status" aria-label="Loading"></loading-spinner>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-size` | `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl` | `m` | Spinner diameter and stroke: xs 0.75em, s 1em, m 1.5em, l 2.5em, xl 4em (em-relative, so it scales with the surrounding text). |
| `data-variant` | `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `error` |  | Arc colour from a theme token (--color-interactive / -success / -warning / -error). Without it the arc uses currentColor. |
| `data-overlay` | boolean |  | position: absolute; inset: 0 over the nearest positioned ancestor, with a translucent surface backdrop and the spinner centered. The container must have a non-static position. |

## CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--spinner-size` | Spinner diameter (default 1.5em; data-size presets override). |
| `--spinner-width` | Ring stroke width (default 0.2em). |
| `--spinner-color` | Arc colour (default currentColor). |
| `--spinner-track` | Track colour (default the arc colour at 20% alpha). |
| `--spinner-speed` | Duration of one rotation (default 0.7s; 1.5s under reduced motion). |

---

# <markdown-editor>

Side-by-side markdown editor with live preview. Adopts the authored textarea and composes markdown-viewer.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/markdown-editor/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<label for="notes">Notes</label>
<markdown-editor>
  <textarea id="notes"># Hello world

Start editing to see a live preview.</textarea>
</markdown-editor>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | string |  | Textarea placeholder; overrides the textarea's own. No default placeholder |
| `rows` | number | `10` | Textarea rows; overrides the textarea's own rows |
| `highlight` | boolean |  | Pass highlight attribute to the preview viewer (markdown-viewer:highlight per code block) |
| `data-tab-indent` | boolean |  | Tab inserts two spaces instead of moving focus. Escape then Tab moves focus; Shift+Tab is never captured. Read at upgrade |
| `data-auto-mermaid` | boolean |  | Upgrade ```mermaid fences in the live preview to diagram-wc (loads the mermaid bridge) |
| `data-theme` | string |  | Theme propagated to the preview pane |
| `data-label-source` | string | `Markdown source` | Accessible name of the source pane; also names the textarea when nothing else does |
| `data-label-preview` | string | `Rendered preview` | Accessible name of the preview pane |
| `data-label-tab-hint` | string | `Tab inserts spaces. Press Escape, then Tab, to move focus.` | Description read with the textarea when data-tab-indent is set |
| `data-editing` | boolean |  | Present when textarea is focused |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | textarea | string |  | Form field name. Goes on the textarea, so the value submits with or without JavaScript |
| `required` | textarea | boolean |  | Native constraint validation (also minlength, maxlength, readonly, form) |
| `id` | textarea | string |  | Kept on upgrade, so a <label for> keeps naming the textarea |
| `dir` | textarea | string |  | Base direction for the source and the preview (default auto) |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `textarea` | The editable source. Adopted and moved into the source pane with its attributes; created when absent |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `markdown-editor:input` | `{ value }` | Fired on each keystroke. Bubbles, composed |
| `markdown-editor:change` | `{ value, source }` | source "user": on blur after the content changed. source "api": when .value is assigned (the next blur does not repeat it). Not fired by form reset. Bubbles, composed |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | Get/set the markdown. Setting updates the preview immediately and fires markdown-editor:change with source "api" |
| `textarea` | `HTMLTextAreaElement` | The backing textarea: the authored one when provided. Stable across reconnects |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Native form controls
- You provide: A <label for> pointing at the authored <textarea>; without one the textarea is named "Markdown source"
- The component manages: `role="group"`, `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Insert two spaces instead of moving focus | Focus in the textarea with data-tab-indent set |
| `Escape` | Release the next Tab press so it moves focus out of the textarea | Focus in the textarea with data-tab-indent set |

---

# <markdown-viewer>

Render markdown content with progressive enhancement. Supports external files, inline content, pluggable parsers, and VB theme integration.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/markdown-viewer/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<markdown-viewer>
  <pre>
# Hello world

This is **inline** markdown with a graceful fallback.
The raw text is visible if JS is disabled.
  </pre>
</markdown-viewer>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | string |  | URL of external markdown file |
| `allow-cross-origin` | boolean |  | Permit a src on another origin (CORS still applies; content is still sanitized unless sanitize="off"). Without it src must be same-origin http(s); redirects are re-checked |
| `sanitize` | `on`, `off`, `false` | `on` | Sanitizing is on unless this is "off" or "false" (any other value, or no attribute, keeps it on). Off writes parser output raw with innerHTML: trusted first-party markdown only, never with a cross-origin or user-influenced src |
| `highlight` | boolean |  | Fire per-block markdown-viewer:highlight events after render |
| `ping` | string |  | URL to ping with render metadata via sendBeacon |
| `data-theme` | string |  | Theme name propagated to .md-content container |
| `data-label-error` | string | `Failed to load markdown` | Text of the role="alert" message shown when src fails to load or parse and no <pre> fallback is visible |
| `data-auto-mermaid` | boolean |  | Upgrade ```mermaid fences in the rendered output to <diagram-wc> (main.js loads the markdown-mermaid bridge when present) |
| `data-rendered` | boolean |  | Present after successful render |
| `data-loading` | boolean |  | Present while fetching external content |
| `data-error` | boolean |  | Present if fetch or parse fails |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `markdown-viewer:fetch` | `{ src }` | Fired when external fetch begins |
| `markdown-viewer:rendered` | `{ src, node }` | Fired after parse and render complete |
| `markdown-viewer:highlight` | `{ node, language }` | Fired per code block when highlight attribute is set |
| `markdown-viewer:error` | `{ error }` | Fired on fetch or parse failure |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `render()` | Force a re-render from the current content source |
| `reload()` | Re-fetch the src URL and re-render |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parser` | `Function\|null` | Custom parser function (markdown string → HTML string). Overrides the default marked parser. Its output is still sanitized unless sanitize="off" |
| `markdown` | `string` | Get the current markdown source, or set a string to render it instead of the slots/src (null or '' falls back to them) |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Live region
- You provide: A fallback <pre> child if the raw source should stay readable when rendering fails
- The component manages: `role="note"`, `role="alert"`

---

# <mobile-menu>

Breakpoint observer for a header menu. Sets [data-mobile] at or below the breakpoint, which shows the author's trigger and hides sibling nav, nav-bar and site-tools in the parent header; a sibling marked data-mobile-menu is moved into the panel instead. The author supplies the trigger and the native popover panel.

- CSS-only custom element. Works without JavaScript.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/custom-elements/mobile-menu/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<header class="site" data-sticky>
  <a href="/"><brand-mark>Acme Inc</brand-mark></a>

  <nav class="horizontal pills" aria-label="Main navigation">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="/about">About</a></li>
      <li><a href="/docs">Docs</a></li>
      <li><a href="/blog">Blog</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>

  <site-tools>
    <site-search>
      <button type="button" data-trigger class="ghost">Search</button>
    </site-search>
  </site-tools>

  <mobile-menu breakpoint="52rem">
    <button type="button" data-trigger
            popovertarget="main-menu" aria-label="Menu">
      <icon-wc name="menu"></icon-wc>
    </button>

    <!-- Panel lives inside mobile-menu so its styles apply -->
    <nav popover id="main-menu" class="mobile-menu-panel"
         aria-label="Site menu">
      <button type="button" class="mobile-menu-close"
              popovertarget="main-menu"
              popovertargetaction="hide" aria-label="Close menu">
        <icon-wc name="x"></icon-wc>
      </button>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/about">About</a></li>
        <li><a href="/docs" aria-current="page">Docs</a></li>
        <li><a href="/blog">Blog</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </mobile-menu>
</header>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `breakpoint` | string | `52rem` | Viewport max-width (CSS length) at or below which mobile mode activates. Observed: changing it re-evaluates. The default 52rem also applies via a CSS media query before upgrade. |
| `data-mobile` | boolean |  | Set by the element while mobile mode is active. Read-only state for styling. |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<button data-trigger popovertarget>` | Author-supplied menu toggle; popovertarget names the panel's id. Give it an aria-label. |
| `<nav popover class="mobile-menu-panel">` | Author-supplied native popover panel, placed inside <mobile-menu> so the link styles apply. Label it (aria-label). Esc closes and focus returns to the trigger; it is not modal (no focus trap or scroll lock). |
| `<button class="mobile-menu-close" popovertargetaction="hide">` | Optional author-supplied close button inside the panel. |
| `<… data-mobile-menu>` | A sibling of <mobile-menu> in the header that should exist once (a notification bell). Moved into the panel in mobile mode and back on leaving it. If it carries data-unread, the trigger shows a dot. |
| `<… data-mobile-menu-slot>` | Optional element inside the panel that receives the moved data-mobile-menu siblings (default: the end of the panel). |

## CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--mobile-menu-bg` | Panel background color |
| `--mobile-menu-radius` | Panel border radius |
| `--mobile-menu-shadow` | Panel box shadow |
| `--mobile-menu-padding` | Panel padding |
| `--mobile-menu-max-width` | Panel maximum width |
| `--mobile-menu-backdrop` | Backdrop overlay color |

---

# <nav-bar>

Top-level site/app navigation primitive. HTML-first wrap or JSON-first .items setter; auto aria-current sync via URL matching (origin + normalised pathname) on popstate and Navigation API entry changes.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/nav-bar/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<nav-bar aria-label="Main">
  <a href="/">Home</a>
  <a href="/docs/">Docs</a>
  <a href="/docs/elements/">Elements</a>
  <a href="/changelog/">Changelog</a>
</nav-bar>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | string |  | Accessible name for the navigation region. |
| `data-match` | `exact` |  | Pathname matching strictness. 'exact' requires exact match. Default: exact wins, longest prefix breaks ties, first-in-DOM-order breaks remaining ties. |
| `data-label-new-tab` | string |  | Screen-reader suffix appended to external .items links. Default: '(opens in new tab)'. |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | a | string |  | Standard anchor href. Resolved against the document base URL and matched by origin + normalised pathname (trailing slash, query and hash ignored). |
| `data-route` | a | string |  | Optional .current target. Falls back to href when absent. |
| `data-nav-link` | a | boolean |  | Marks a descendant <a> as a candidate for active-state matching when the link list is wrapped (e.g. inside <li> or <drop-down>). When any descendant carries this attribute, those replace 'direct children' as the candidate set. When none of them matches the location but a link nested beside one does (a menu item in the same <drop-down> or <li>), that one gets aria-current="true" as the current section. |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nav-bar:upgraded` |  | Fired after every connect, including reconnects after a move. |
| `nav-bar:items-changed` | `{ items, source: 'property' }` | Fired after .items is assigned a new (not deep-equal) value. |
| `nav-bar:current-changed` | `{ current, previous, source: 'property' \| 'popstate' \| 'navigation' \| 'pathname' }` | Fired when the active link changes. |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `releaseCurrent()` | Drop explicit ownership of .current and re-run URL matching. |
| `refresh()` | Re-run URL matching manually (for routers that change the URL without popstate or the Navigation API). No-op while .current is explicitly owned. |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<{ href, label, route?, icon?, external?, badge? }>` | Read returns the last assigned array, else { href, label } inferred from the managed links. Assigning replaces the direct <a> children with the default renderer (deep-equal assignment is a no-op). Only http(s) and relative hrefs render as links. |
| `current` | `string \| null` | Read returns the active route (data-route or href of the aria-current link, or the explicit value). Assigning takes ownership: URL sync stops until releaseCurrent(). |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Landmark navigation
- You provide: An aria-label on the host, or on the wrapped <nav>, that names the navigation
- The component manages: `role="navigation"`, `aria-current`

---

# <note-wc>

Private reader notes on highlights: a note action inside selection-menu, a page-level button with for="id", and the note panel itself. Also opens the panel for margin-annotation clicks (it listens for highlights:request-note on document).

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/note-wc/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<selection-menu for="my-article">
  <highlight-wc></highlight-wc>
  <note-wc></note-wc>
</selection-menu>

<article id="my-article">
  <p>Select text, click the note icon to highlight and add a note.</p>
</article>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `for` | string |  | ID of the target article (page-level mode). The button opens the panel for the first noted, else first, highlight on it. Without for and outside selection-menu, note-wc renders no button and only hosts the panel. |
| `data-label-add` | string | `Add private note` | Accessible name of the button inside selection-menu. |
| `data-label-view` | string | `View notes` | Accessible name of the page-level (for="id") button. |
| `data-label-dialog` | string | `Private note` | Accessible name of the note panel dialog. |
| `data-label-heading` | string | `Private note` | Visible panel heading (uppercased by CSS). |
| `data-label-placeholder` | string | `Add a note…` | Textarea placeholder. |
| `data-label-textarea` | string | `Note for highlighted text` | Textarea accessible name. |
| `data-label-save` | string | `Save` | Save button text. |
| `data-label-cancel` | string | `Cancel` | Cancel button text. |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `openFor` | openFor(highlight, controller, opener?) opens the note panel for a highlight record on a highlights controller (from initHighlights). Focus returns to opener (default: the element focused when it opened) on close. The highlights:request-note document event calls this on the first connected note-wc. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Dialog (non-modal)
- The component manages: `role="dialog"`, `aria-label`, `aria-hidden`, `tabindex`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Close the note panel without saving and return focus to the opener (or the highlight when the opener is gone) | Focus in the note panel |
| `Ctrl+Enter` / `Meta+Enter` | Save the note and close the panel | Focus in the note textarea |

---

# <notification-wc>

Dual-mode notification component: dismissible banner or bell-icon panel with history + read tracking.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/notification-wc/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<notification-wc mode="banner" persist="site-update-v3" variant="info" position="top">
  <strong>v3.0 is out.</strong> <a href="/changelog">See what's new</a>
  <button type="button" value="dismiss" aria-label="Dismiss">
    <icon-wc name="x" size="sm"></icon-wc>
  </button>
</notification-wc>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `banner`, `panel` |  | Which presentation mode to render (default: panel) |
| `persist` | string |  | Banner mode: VBStore key used to record dismiss state |
| `variant` | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error` |  | Banner mode: color variant (reactive) |
| `position` | `top`, `bottom` |  | Banner mode: top = sticky to the viewport top, bottom = fixed to the viewport bottom (reactive) |
| `expires` | number |  | Banner mode: days until the banner re-shows after dismiss |
| `src` | string |  | Panel mode: absolute or root-relative URL, or a VBService role name, for dynamic notifications |
| `poll` | number |  | Panel mode: polling interval in milliseconds |
| `toast-new` | string |  | Panel mode: on each poll after the first, show a toast for every never-seen dynamic notification on the <toast-msg> matched by the value (a selector, e.g. #id); bare, invalid, or no matching <toast-msg> = first <toast-msg> in the document |
| `storage-key` | string |  | Panel mode: VBStore namespace for read state (default: notifications) |
| `data-label-trigger` | string | `Notifications` | Panel mode: Trigger accessible name (minted bell; an authored trigger keeps its own name). |
| `data-label-unread` | string | `{n} unread` | Panel mode: Unread count appended to the trigger name ({n} = count). |
| `data-label-title` | string | `Notifications` | Panel mode: Panel heading and dialog name. |
| `data-label-mark-all` | string | `Mark all read` | Panel mode: Mark-all button text. |
| `data-label-close` | string | `Close notifications` | (panel) Accessible name of the close button shown when the panel opens as a sheet |
| `data-label-tabs` | string | `Notification categories` | Panel mode: Tab list accessible name. |
| `data-label-all` | string | `All` | Panel mode: All tab text. |
| `data-label-watching` | string | `Watching` | Panel mode: Watching tab text. |
| `data-label-empty` | string | `No notifications` | Panel mode: Empty-state text for the All tab. |
| `data-label-watch-empty` | string | `You aren’t watching any pages yet. Use the “Watch” button on a page to start.` | Panel mode: Empty-state text for the Watching tab. |
| `data-label-last-checked` | string | `Last checked: {date}` | Panel mode: Watch row check time ({date} = formatted date). |
| `data-label-never` | string | `—` | Panel mode: Watch row check time when never checked. |
| `data-label-changed` | string | `Changed` | Panel mode: Badge on watched pages whose content changed. |
| `data-label-unwatch` | string | `Unwatch {title}` | Panel mode: Unwatch button accessible name ({title} = page title). |
| `data-label-new` | string | `New notification` | Panel mode: Toast text when a new notification has no title or body. |
| `data-label-added` | string | `New notification: {title}. {n} unread` | Panel mode: Text announced to screen readers when a notification arrives after the page has loaded ({title} = its title, {n} = unread count). |
| `data-label-variant-info` | string | `Information:` | Banner mode: visually hidden prefix announcing the info variant, so it isn't conveyed by colour alone. |
| `data-label-variant-success` | string | `Success:` | Banner mode: visually hidden prefix announcing the success variant, so it isn't conveyed by colour alone. |
| `data-label-variant-warning` | string | `Warning:` | Banner mode: visually hidden prefix announcing the warning variant, so it isn't conveyed by colour alone. |
| `data-label-variant-error` | string | `Error:` | Banner mode: visually hidden prefix announcing the error variant, so it isn't conveyed by colour alone. |
| `data-unread` | number |  | (panel) Set by the element to the unread count while there are unread items, removed at zero. Read-only state for styling from outside (a mobile-menu trigger's unread dot). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-trigger` | button | boolean |  | Panel mode: marks an authored trigger button that replaces the minted bell. An unread badge is appended inside it. |
| `data-id` | article | string |  | Panel mode: notification id (read state and dynamic merge key). |
| `data-type` | article | `update`, `alert`, `watch`, `system`, `message`, `stewardship` |  | Panel mode: row icon (default update). |
| `data-date` | article | string |  | Panel mode: ISO date; sorts rows newest first and is shown formatted in the document language. |
| `value` | button | string |  | Banner mode: value="dismiss" (or data-dismiss) marks the dismiss button. |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notification-wc:new` | `{ notification }` | A never-seen entry arrived in a dynamic fetch |
| `notification-wc:read` | `{ id }` | An entry was marked read |
| `notification-wc:dismiss` | `{ id }` | Banner was dismissed (id = persist key) |
| `notification-wc:open` |  | Panel opened |
| `notification-wc:close` |  | Panel closed |
| `notification-wc:notifications-changed` | `{ notifications, source: 'property' }` | The notifications setter replaced the dynamic list |
| `page-watch:remove` | `{ url, subscriptionId }` | A page was unwatched from the Watching tab |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications` | `Array<{ id, title, body?, date?, type?, url?, dismissed? }>` | Panel mode: dynamic notifications merged over static <article> children by id (same shape as the src feed). The getter returns a copy; the setter re-renders and fires notification-wc:notifications-changed. url renders as a link only when it resolves to http(s). Banner mode ignores the setter. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Non-modal dialog with tabs
- You provide: In banner mode, a dismiss button with an accessible name; in panel mode, an accessible name on an authored trigger
- The component manages: `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-label`, `role="dialog"`, `role="status"`, `role="alert"`, `aria-labelledby`, `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`, `aria-selected`, `tabindex`, `role="list"`, `aria-hidden`, `hidden`, `popover`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Close the panel and return focus to the trigger | Panel open and focus on the trigger or inside the panel |
| `ArrowRight` | Move to and select the next tab, wrapping (reversed in right-to-left) | Focus on a tab |
| `ArrowLeft` | Move to and select the previous tab, wrapping (reversed in right-to-left) | Focus on a tab |
| `Home` | Move to and select the first tab | Focus on a tab |
| `End` | Move to and select the last tab | Focus on a tab |

---

# <page-info>

Document provenance disclosure panel

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/page-info/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<page-info>
  <details>
    <summary>
      <span class="page-info-author">Jane Doe</span>
      <span class="page-info-sep" aria-hidden="true">&middot;</span>
      <time datetime="2026-03-15" data-relative>
        15 March 2026
      </time>
      <span class="page-info-sep" aria-hidden="true">&middot;</span>
      <span class="page-info-badge"
            data-provenance="ai-assisted"
            data-trust="declared">
        Human-written, AI-assisted
      </span>
    </summary>
    <section class="page-info-panel">
      <section>
        <h2 class="page-info-section-heading">Author</h2>
        <ul class="page-info-author-list">
          <li>
            <address>
              <a href="/team/jane" rel="author">Jane Doe</a>
              <span class="page-info-role">Lead author</span>
            </address>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </section>
      <section>
        <h2 class="page-info-section-heading">History</h2>
        <dl>
          <div>
            <dt>Published</dt>
            <dd><time datetime="2026-01-10">January 10, 2026</time></dd>
          </div>
          <div>
            <dt>Last updated</dt>
            <dd>
              <time datetime="2026-03-15" data-relative>
                15 March 2026
              </time>
            </dd>
          </div>
          <div>
            <dt>Version</dt>
            <dd>1.4.0</dd>
          </div>
          <div>
            <dt>Reading time</dt>
            <dd data-reading-time>&mdash;</dd>
          </div>
        </dl>
      </section>
      <section>
        <h2 class="page-info-section-heading">How this was made</h2>
        <dl>
          <div>
            <dt>Authorship</dt>
            <dd>Human-written, AI-assisted</dd>
          </div>
          <div>
            <dt>AI tools used</dt>
            <dd>Claude Sonnet 4 &mdash; research and drafting</dd>
          </div>
          <div>
            <dt>Review</dt>
            <dd>Editor-reviewed</dd>
          </div>
        </dl>
      </section>
    </section>
  </details>
</page-info>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | boolean |  | Render the whole panel from <meta> tags in <head> (meta-tag contract v1): author, link[rel=author] / article:author, last-modified / article:modified_time, article:published_time, itemprop=version, vb:version-url, vb:provenance, vb:ai-tools, vb:review, vb:status, license + link[rel=license], keywords, repeated meta[name=concept]. Values are inserted as text; links are used only when they resolve to http(s). |
| `data-concept-base` | string | `/topics/` | Auto mode: base path for concept links ({base}{id}/). Must be relative or http(s); otherwise concepts render as plain text. |
| `data-heading-level` | `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6` | `2` | Auto mode: heading level of the panel section headings. |
| `data-label-reading-time` | string | `~{n}` | Template for [data-reading-time]; {n} is the Intl-formatted minute value ("5 min"). |
| `data-label-author` | string | `Author` | Auto mode UI string (default "Author"). |
| `data-label-history` | string | `History` | Auto mode UI string (default "History"). |
| `data-label-provenance` | string | `How this was made` | Auto mode UI string (default "How this was made"). |
| `data-label-topic` | string | `Topic` | Auto mode UI string (default "Topic"). |
| `data-label-published` | string | `Published` | Auto mode UI string (default "Published"). |
| `data-label-updated` | string | `Last updated` | Auto mode UI string (default "Last updated"). |
| `data-label-version` | string | `Version` | Auto mode UI string (default "Version"). |
| `data-label-authorship` | string | `Authorship` | Auto mode UI string (default "Authorship"). |
| `data-label-ai-tools` | string | `AI tools used` | Auto mode UI string (default "AI tools used"). |
| `data-label-review` | string | `Review` | Auto mode UI string (default "Review"). |
| `data-label-status` | string | `Status` | Auto mode UI string (default "Status"). |
| `data-label-license` | string | `License` | Auto mode UI string (default "License"). |
| `data-label-concepts` | string | `Concepts` | Auto mode UI string (default "Concepts"). |
| `data-label-keywords` | string | `Keywords` | Auto mode UI string (default "Keywords"). |
| `data-label-tier-declared` | string | `Self-declared` | Visible trust-tier text appended to the badge for data-trust="declared" (default "Self-declared"). |
| `data-label-tier-verified` | string | `Verified` | Visible trust-tier text appended to the badge for data-trust="verified" (default "Verified"). |
| `data-label-tier-failed` | string | `Signature failed` | Visible trust-tier text appended to the badge for data-trust="failed" (default "Signature failed"). |
| `data-label-tier-key-unavailable` | string | `Key unavailable` | Visible trust-tier text appended to the badge for data-trust="key-unavailable" (default "Key unavailable"). |
| `data-label-tier-key-untrusted` | string | `Key not from this site` | Visible trust-tier text for data-trust="failed" when link[rel=author-key] points at another origin (default "Key not from this site"). The key is not fetched. |
| `data-label-tier-key-expired` | string | `Key expired` | Visible trust-tier text for data-trust="failed" when the key's metadata.expires date has passed (default "Key expired"). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-trust` | .page-info-badge | `undeclared`, `declared`, `verified`, `failed`, `key-unavailable` |  | Verification tier, written by the component (the first .page-info-badge without data-status). A .page-info-tier span with the tier text is appended inside the badge. |
| `data-provenance` | .page-info-badge | string |  | vb:provenance token(s) the badge describes (styling hook). |
| `data-status` | .page-info-badge | `draft`, `archived` |  | Publication-status badge (auto mode renders it for non-published pages); excluded from trust updates. |
| `data-relative` | time | boolean |  | Rewrite the text as a localized relative time (Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, closest [lang]) from the datetime attribute; the absolute date is put in title unless the author set one. Future dates read "in 3 days". |
| `datetime` | time | string |  | ISO date or datetime read by time[data-relative]. Date-only values are formatted in UTC. |
| `data-reading-time` | any element | boolean |  | Filled with the estimated reading time of the page's outermost [data-signable] roots (238 wpm / 500 CJK chars per minute, shared with page-stats; skips [data-signable=false], hidden and script content). |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `details` | Static mode: <details> with a <summary> trust bar (author as plain text, time[data-relative], .page-info-badge) and a .page-info-panel of sections. Keep links out of <summary>. |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page-info:verified` | `{ status: 'undeclared' \| 'declared' \| 'verified' \| 'failed' \| 'key-unavailable', tier: 0 \| 1 \| 3 \| -1 \| -2, reason?: string }` | Bubbles. Fired on every setup with the declared tier (undeclared/declared, no reason), then again with the verification result when the page carries meta[name=vb:signature]. reason: 'ok', 'mismatch', 'hash-mismatch' (vb:hash differs from the canonical document), 'key-origin' (key is not same-origin), 'key-expired', 'missing-author-key', 'unsupported-algorithm:…', 'canonicalize:…', 'verify:…', or the key fetch error. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Native details/summary
- The component manages: `aria-label`, `aria-hidden`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Open or close the page information panel | Native behaviour of summary |

---

# <page-stats>

Lightweight reading statistics

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/page-stats/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<page-stats data-for="article-content" data-show="reading-time,word-count"></page-stats>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-for` | string |  | ID of the target content element to analyze. Without it (or with an author-rendered <dl> inside) the component renders nothing and adopts the existing markup. |
| `data-wpm` | number | `238` | Words per minute for reading time (default 238, shared with page-info). Chinese/Japanese text is timed at 500 characters per minute. |
| `data-show` | string | `reading-time` | Comma-separated list of stats to display, in fixed order: reading-time, word-count, last-modified. Unknown tokens are ignored. last-modified reads meta[name=last-modified], then meta[property=article:modified_time]; it is omitted when neither is present. |
| `data-label-reading-time` | string | `Reading time` | Visually hidden dt label for the reading-time item. |
| `data-label-word-count` | string | `Word count` | Visually hidden dt label for the word-count item. |
| `data-label-last-modified` | string | `Last updated` | Visually hidden dt label for the last-modified item. |
| `data-label-min-read` | string | `{n} read` | Reading-time text template; {n} is the Intl-formatted minute value ("5 min"). Default "{n} read" for English documents, "{n}" otherwise. |
| `data-label-words` | string | `{n} words` | Word-count text template; {n} is the Intl-formatted count. Per-plural overrides: data-label-words-zero/-one/-two/-few/-many (Intl.PluralRules category of the document language). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-generated` | dl | boolean |  | Set by the component on the <dl> it renders itself. A <dl> without it is author/SSR markup and is adopted unchanged. |
| `data-stats-ignore` | any element inside the target | boolean |  | Exclude this subtree from the word count (script, style, template, noscript, [hidden], [aria-hidden=true] and [inert] are always excluded). |

---

# <page-toc>

Table of contents with scroll-spy

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/page-toc/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<section data-toc-ignore>
  <h2>Demo Heading</h2>
  <p>This heading will not appear in the ToC.</p>
</section>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | string | `h2,h3` | Comma-separated heading levels to include (auto-generated mode) |
| `scope` | string | `main` | CSS selector for the container whose headings are scanned (first match wins; docs layouts use 'main article') |
| `data-title` | string | `On this page` | Summary text and nav aria-label of the generated ToC |
| `orientation` | `horizontal` |  | 'horizontal' renders an inline, horizontally scrollable bar (summary hidden, nesting flattened). Omit for the default vertical tree |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-toc-ignore` | heading (or any ancestor) inside the scope container | boolean |  | Exclude the heading, or every heading inside the marked container, from the generated ToC |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page-toc:navigate` | `{ id }` | Fired when a ToC link is activated; id is the target heading's id |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh` | Rebuild the ToC (auto mode) or re-scan authored links (manual mode) after content changes |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` | `Array<{ id?: string, text: string, level: number }>` | Current ToC entries derived from the page headings |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Landmark navigation
- You provide: Headings that have an id and text content inside the scoped container
- The component manages: `aria-label`, `aria-current`, `tabindex`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Scroll to the heading and move focus to it | Native behaviour of a link; the component handles the click |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Collapse or expand the whole table of contents | Native behaviour of summary |

# <page-tools>

Configurable toolbar for page-level utilities

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/page-tools/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<aside>
  <page-toc levels="h2,h3" scope="article"></page-toc>
  <page-tools data-position="sticky">
    <print-page></print-page>
    <share-wc variant="icon" size="s"></share-wc>
  </page-tools>
</aside>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-position` | `sticky`, `fixed`, `inline` | `sticky` | Positioning strategy |
| `data-orientation` | `auto`, `vertical`, `horizontal` | `auto` | Tool strip direction; auto resolves to horizontal for inline, vertical otherwise. Re-resolved when changed |
| `data-gap` | `2xs`, `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l` | `s` | Gap token between tools |
| `data-fab-icon` | string | `ellipsis-vertical` | Icon name for the mobile FAB |
| `data-fab-label` | string | `Page tools` | Accessible label for the FAB and its popover panel |
| `data-breakpoint` | string | `48rem` | Viewport width at or below which the toolbar collapses to a FAB |
| `data-resolved-orientation` | `vertical`, `horizontal` |  | Reflected effective orientation (data-orientation resolved against data-position) |
| `data-collapsed` | boolean |  | Present while the toolbar is collapsed to the FAB (viewport at or below data-breakpoint) |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `button.page-tools-fab` | Generated FAB (popovertarget → panel); visible only while collapsed. Internal (data-page-tools-internal) |
| `section.page-tools-popover[popover]` | Generated popover panel that holds the tools while collapsed. Internal (data-page-tools-internal) |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools` | `Element[]` | The tool elements (author children, excluding the generated FAB and popover; read from the popover while collapsed) |

## CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--page-tools-gap` | Gap between tools (set by data-gap) |
| `--page-tools-offset` | Sticky top offset / fixed inline-end offset |
| `--page-tools-button-padding` | Padding of normalised icon tool buttons |
| `--page-tools-icon-size` | Icon size inside tool buttons (default 1.25rem) |
| `--page-tools-fab-size` | FAB diameter (default 3rem) |
| `--page-tools-fab-bottom` | FAB distance from the viewport block-end edge |
| `--page-tools-fab-end` | FAB distance from the viewport inline-end edge |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Toolbar
- You provide: Child controls that each have an accessible name
- The component manages: `role="toolbar"`, `aria-label`, `aria-orientation`, `tabindex`, `aria-hidden`, `popover`, `hidden`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ArrowRight` | Move to the next tool, wrapping (reversed in right-to-left) | Horizontal toolbar |
| `ArrowLeft` | Move to the previous tool, wrapping (reversed in right-to-left) | Horizontal toolbar |
| `ArrowDown` | Move to the next tool, wrapping | Vertical toolbar or collapsed panel |
| `ArrowUp` | Move to the previous tool, wrapping | Vertical toolbar or collapsed panel |
| `Home` | Move to the first tool |  |
| `End` | Move to the last tool |  |
| `Escape` | Close the collapsed panel and return focus to the floating button | Native behaviour of popover |
