# <watch-wc>

Drop-in wrapper for the data-watch-page button. Renders an icon, compact, or full-button toggle (aria-pressed) that adds or removes the current page from the user's VBStore('watches') list. The state machine lives in src/utils/page-watch-init.js; the component repaints its label, icon and title from the button's aria-pressed.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/watch-wc/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<watch-wc></watch-wc>                          <!-- icon (default) -->
<watch-wc variant="compact"></watch-wc>        <!-- small icon + text -->
<watch-wc variant="button"></watch-wc>         <!-- full ghost button -->
<watch-wc variant="button" label="Save for later"></watch-wc>  <!-- constant label -->
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `icon`, `compact`, `button` | `icon` | Visual preset. icon is named by aria-label (data-label-action); compact and button are named by their visible text. Changing it after upgrade re-renders. |
| `label` | string |  | Constant visible text for the compact and button variants, used in both states (overrides data-label-watch / data-label-watching). Ignored by the icon variant. |
| `server-sync` | boolean |  | Turns on server-side sync via VBService('notify') for the whole page: sets the page-global window.vbPageWatch.serverSync flag, which every watch button (and the notification panel's unwatch) uses from then on. Equivalent to <meta name="vb-page-watch-server" content="true">. |
| `data-label-watch` | string | `Watch for updates` | Visible text (and accessible name) of the compact/button variants while the page is not watched. Localisation hook. |
| `data-label-watching` | string | `Watching` | Visible text (and accessible name) of the compact/button variants while the page is watched. Localisation hook. |
| `data-label-action` | string | `Watch this page for updates` | Icon variant: the button's aria-label, and its tooltip while not watched. Localisation hook. |
| `data-label-stop` | string | `Stop watching this page` | Icon variant: tooltip while the page is watched. Localisation hook. |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `button[data-watch-page][data-watch-wc]` | Generated toggle button with aria-pressed; icon variant carries aria-label, text variants a <span> label |
| `icon-wc` | bookmark / bookmark-check icon, aria-hidden |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page-watch:add` | `[object Object]` | Bubbles from the inner button when the user starts watching |
| `page-watch:remove` | `[object Object]` | Bubbles from the inner button when the user stops watching (also dispatched by notification-wc's Watching tab) |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Button
- The component manages: `aria-pressed`, `aria-label`, `aria-hidden`, `title`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Start or stop watching the page | Native behaviour of button |

---

# <week-view>

Week time grid composing day-view-style columns in a semantic table. Defaults to the current week (locale first day); today's header has aria-current="date". Changing data-start-date, data-days, data-start-hour, data-end-hour or a data-label-* after upgrade rebuilds a generated table.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/week-view/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<week-view data-start-date="2026-04-06">
  <calendar-event data-date="2026-04-06" data-category="meeting">
    <time datetime="09:00">9:00 AM</time>
    Sprint standup
  </calendar-event>
  <calendar-event data-date="2026-04-07" data-category="focus" data-duration="2h">
    <time datetime="10:00">10:00 AM</time>
    Design review
  </calendar-event>
  <calendar-event data-date="2026-04-09" data-category="deadline">
    <time datetime="16:00">4:00 PM</time>
    Sprint deadline
  </calendar-event>
</week-view>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-start-date` | string |  | ISO date for the first day of the view (e.g., 2026-04-06). Default: the current week, starting on the locale's first day of week (Intl.Locale weekInfo, closest [lang]). |
| `data-days` | number | `7` | Number of day columns, clamped to 1-14 (e.g., 5 for a workweek). Invalid values fall back to 7. |
| `data-start-hour` | string | `auto` | First visible hour (0-23), or 'auto' to scan events. A fixed range grows to fit events outside it. |
| `data-end-hour` | number | `19` | Last visible hour (0-23). Ignored when data-start-hour is 'auto'. |
| `data-label-continues` | string | `continues after the visible hours` | Text appended to the accessible name of a spanning event that runs past the last visible hour (localisation hook). |
| `data-label-time` | string | `Time` | Visually hidden name of the corner header over the hour labels (localisation hook). |

## Attributes on children

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-date` | calendar-event | string |  | ISO date assigning this event to a day column (auto mode). Events outside the range, or without a time, are not placed and are hidden. |
| `data-duration` | calendar-event | string |  | Makes the event span hour rows. Durations (data-duration): 2h, 1.5h, 45m, 90m, 1h30m, bare minutes (60), ISO-8601 (PT1H30M); unparseable values fall back to 1 hour. Overlapping spans in one day column are laid out side by side. |
| `data-continues` | calendar-event | boolean |  | Set by the component (not authored) on a spanning event clipped at the last visible hour. |

## Structure

| Child | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `table` | Semantic table: hours (rows) × days (columns) |
| `thead > tr > th` | Day column headers: <time datetime> with a short visible date (month added when the range crosses one) and a visually hidden full date; today's has aria-current="date" |
| `tbody > tr > th` | Hour row headers with <time datetime='HH:00'> |
| `tbody > tr > td` | Day/hour cell containing hour-view and calendar-event elements |
| `hour-view` | Subgrid container for events within a cell |
| `calendar-event` | Individual event with time, category, and optional duration |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `week-view:event-click` | `{ date, time, text, element, category, duration }` | Fired when a calendar-event is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused |
| `week-view:events-changed` | `{ events, source: 'property' }` | Fired after the events property rebuilds the view |

## Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh()` | Re-measure and re-position spanning events now (they also re-position automatically when the view resizes) |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `events` | `Array<{ date?, time, text, category?, duration? }>` | Get the week's events as data (including unplaced ones outside the range), or assign an array to rebuild the table. time is HH:MM or a full ISO datetime (its date is used when date is omitted). Durations (data-duration): 2h, 1.5h, 45m, 90m, 1h30m, bare minutes (60), ISO-8601 (PT1H30M); unparseable values fall back to 1 hour. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Native table with roving focus across events
- You provide: Child <calendar-event> elements with a data-date and a <time>, each with text that names the event
- The component manages: `role="button"`, `role="group"`, `aria-label`, `aria-current`, `aria-hidden`, `tabindex roving`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ArrowDown` | Move to the next event in the same day | Focus on an event |
| `ArrowUp` | Move to the previous event in the same day | Focus on an event |
| `ArrowRight` | Move to the closest event in time in the next day that has events (reversed in right-to-left) | Focus on an event |
| `ArrowLeft` | Move to the closest event in time in the previous day that has events (reversed in right-to-left) | Focus on an event |
| `Home` | Move to the first event in the view | Focus on an event |
| `End` | Move to the last event in the view | Focus on an event |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Fire week-view:event-click for the event | Focus on the event itself, not a link or button inside it |

---

# <youtube-player>

YouTube embed behind a facade: a thumbnail (or local poster) and one play button; the youtube-nocookie.com iframe loads only when the reader presses play. Without poster the thumbnail is requested from i.ytimg.com on render.

- Web component. Needs the Vanilla Breeze script; its children are the fallback when script has not run.
- Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/web-components/youtube-player/
- Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4

## Example

```html
<youtube-player
  video-id="dQw4w9WgXcQ"
  title="Rick Astley — Never Gonna Give You Up">
</youtube-player>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `video-id` | string |  | YouTube video ID (6–20 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -). Missing or invalid: the element does not upgrade and the authored fallback stays. |
| `title` | string | `YouTube video` | Video title: the iframe title and the {title} in the play-button name. |
| `start` | number |  | Start playback at N seconds. Whole non-negative seconds only; anything else is ignored with a console warning. |
| `end` | number |  | Stop playback at N seconds. Whole non-negative seconds only. |
| `list` | string |  | YouTube playlist ID. |
| `params` | string |  | Extra query string for the embed URL (escape hatch); its keys override start, end, list and autoplay. The embed host is fixed. |
| `autoplay` | boolean |  | Load the iframe on connect instead of the facade (this contacts YouTube at once). Ignored under prefers-reduced-motion or data-motion-reduced. Never moves focus. |
| `thumbnail` | `hq`, `mq`, `sd`, `maxres` | `hq` | i.ytimg.com thumbnail size. sd and maxres fall back to hq when the video has none. |
| `poster` | string |  | Local image URL for the facade. When set, no thumbnail is requested from i.ytimg.com; nothing contacts Google until play. |
| `data-label-play` | string | `Play {title}` | Accessible name of the play button; {title} is replaced with the title. |
| `state` | `ready`, `active` |  | Set by the component: ready = facade shown, active = iframe inserted. Reconnect (move or reinsert) renders the facade again. |

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `youtube-player:activate` | `{ videoId: string, fromUser: boolean }` | Fired (bubbles) when the iframe is inserted; fromUser is false for the autoplay attribute. |
| `youtube-player:upgraded` |  | Fired (bubbles) after the element upgrades. |

## Accessibility

- Pattern: Button
- You provide: A title attribute naming the video; it names the play button and the player frame
- The component manages: `aria-label`, `title`

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Load the video and move focus to the player frame | Native behaviour of button |

---

# Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4: themes

A theme changes colour, type, shape and shadow for the whole page or for one element and its descendants. Pick one that suits the content; do not restyle components by hand to get a look a theme already provides.

## Use a theme

```html
<html lang="en" data-theme="modern">
```

Colour scheme is separate: `data-mode="light"` or `data-mode="dark"` on `<html>` forces one; without it the page follows the visitor's system setting. Every theme has both.

## Core themes (in the main stylesheet)

- `default`: The VB default — balanced blue-purple palette
- `modern`: Vibrant & elevated — tech-forward with bounce
- `minimal`: Clean & flat — content-focused restraint
- `classic`: Serif & elegant — timeless editorial feel
- `a11y-high-contrast`: AAA contrast (7:1+) for low vision
- `a11y-large-text`: 25% larger fonts and spacing
- `a11y-dyslexia`: Atkinson Hyperlegible with wide spacing

## Accents (in the main stylesheet)

An accent swaps the brand hues and keeps everything else. It is a separate attribute, so it combines with a theme: `<html data-theme="modern" data-accent="forest">`.

- `ocean`: Cool oceanic blues with teal undertones
- `forest`: Natural earthy greens with amber accent
- `sunset`: Warm energetic orange-red palette
- `rose`: Warm romantic pinks with ocean accent
- `lavender`: Soft calming purples with golden accent
- `coral`: Warm peachy tones with teal contrast
- `slate`: Cool professional gray-blue palette
- `emerald`: Rich vibrant green with warm accent
- `amber`: Golden warm tones with cool contrast
- `indigo`: Deep rich blues with violet depth

## Standalone themes (one extra stylesheet each)

Add the theme file after the main stylesheet, then set `data-theme`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/vanilla-breeze/dist/cdn/vanilla-breeze.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/vanilla-breeze/dist/cdn/themes/nord.css">
```

- `swiss`: Precision grid typography with Swiss red
- `brutalist`: Raw industrial — monospace, hard shadows
- `art-deco`: Gold + black, geometric shapes — 1920s luxury
- `editorial`: Magazine elegance — serif hierarchy, thin rules
- `genai`: AI startup aesthetic — purple gradients, glow, sparkle
- `glassmorphism`: Frosted glass surfaces — blur, gradients, translucency
- `startup`: Modern SaaS energy — electric indigo, gradient CTAs
- `organic`: Natural handcrafted — warm earthy curves
- `rough`: Hand-drawn sketchbook — pencil lines on warm paper
- `cyber`: Neon futuristic — glowing UI on dark void
- `journal`: Dot-grid paper, washi tape, and handmade warmth
- `vaporwave`: Hot pink/cyan on deep purple — neon glow, retro-dreamy
- `neumorphism`: Soft embossed surfaces — monochromatic double-shadow UI
- `bauhaus`: Geometric precision — primary colors, zero shadows, functional beauty
- `claymorphism`: 3D clay surfaces — puffy pastels, squish interactions
- `alpha1999`: Space retro-fi — amber CRT on deep void
- `super2026`: Supergraphic bold — warm paper, geometric red accents
- `magna`: Magnavox Odyssey 2 retro — rainbow spectrum, chrome text, deep space void
- `8bit`: Retro pixel art — chunky blocks, CRT glow
- `nes`: Console pixels — 4-color palette, beveled frames
- `win9x`: Classic desktop — 3D bevels, system gray
- `kawaii`: Cute aesthetic — pastel pink, bouncy pills
- `memphis`: 1980s bold playfulness — offset shadows, confetti, chaos
- `nord`: Arctic blue-gray — muted palette, calm professional
- `solarized`: Engineered 16-color precision — light/dark symmetry
- `dracula`: Purple bg, cyan/green/pink accents — dark-first elegance
- `catppuccin-mocha`: Warm pastels on tinted dark — cozy, unhurried
- `catppuccin-latte`: Warm pastels on light cream — cozy daytime Catppuccin
- `catppuccin-frappe`: Muted pastels on mid-dark blue — cool Catppuccin twilight
- `catppuccin-macchiato`: Rich pastels on deep blue — the darkest Catppuccin
- `gruvbox`: Earthy retro warmth — warm grays, red/green/yellow/aqua accents
- `tokyo-night`: Deep indigo night-owl — muted blue-purple, bright accent pops
- `rose-pine`: Muted rose/pine/gold — elegant, restrained, expensive
- `cottagecore`: Pastoral warmth — sage green, dusty rose, botanical dividers
- `terminal`: Retro CRT — green phosphor on black
- `clinical`: Sterile precision — medical blue, maximum clarity
- `financial`: Trustworthy authority — navy + gold, serif headings
- `government`: Official USWDS-inspired — navy + red, maximum legibility
- `dawn`: Golden morning light — warm peach/gold/cream, soft and inviting
- `dusk`: Twilight contemplation — purple-blue + warm amber, elongated shadows
- `midnight`: Deep night minimalism — near-black, muted blue, desaturated
- `high-noon`: Maximum brightness — vivid saturated colors, strong shadows

## Your own colours and spacing

When a page needs a rule of its own, write it in a stylesheet with design tokens, never literal values: `var(--color-primary)`, `var(--color-surface)`, `var(--color-text-muted)`, `var(--size-m)` (sizes run `3xs` to `3xl`), `var(--radius-m)`, `var(--shadow-m)`. Tokens follow the theme and the colour scheme.

Documentation: https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/themes/ and https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/tokens/

---

# Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4: attributes

Attributes that work on any element (or on the native elements named in each page). Component-specific attributes are in each component file. Each link is the full documentation page.

## Analytics

- [data-vb-event](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-vb-event/): Declarative analytics — fire a normalised analytics event on click without writing JavaScript. Properties via data-vb-event-* siblings.
- [data-vb-no-track](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-vb-no-track/): Exclude an element (and everything inside it) from Vanilla Breeze analytics. No beacons fire from any descendant, regardless of data-vb-event or auto-wired VB events.

## Clipboard

- [data-copy](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-copy/): Clipboard copy and paste via data attributes. Add data-copy, data-copy-target, or data-paste-target to any button for clipboard functionality with visible, screen-reader and failure feedback.
- [data-highlights](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-highlights/): The text-highlighting engine: renders and persists highlights on any element with the CSS Custom Highlight API. No built-in UI; pair it with highlight-wc and selection-menu for interactive highlighting.

## Content

- [data-provenance](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-provenance/): Declare how content was made — human, AI-assisted, AI-generated, translated, synthesized, or migrated. CSS-only indicators for authorship provenance.
- [data-review](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-review/): Declare what review the content has received. Orthogonal to data-provenance and data-status.
- [data-status](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-status/): Declare content publication state — draft, published, archived. Orthogonal to data-provenance and data-review.
- [data-trust](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-trust/): Verification tier indicator on page-info badges. Runtime-computed state showing whether page content matches its cryptographic signature.
- [data-watch-page](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-watch-page/): Mark a button as the watch toggle for the current page. Stores a content hash; on revisit, fires a watch notification when content has changed.

## Data

- [data-sortable](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-sortable/): Client-side list/table sorting upscale on any container — native ul/ol/table or VB collections. Two API shapes (clickable column headers OR external select/button); composes with data-paged.

## Focus

- [data-focus-trap](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-focus-trap/): Constrain keyboard focus within a container. Tab/Shift+Tab cycle inside the boundary, focus auto-moves in on activation, and restores on deactivation.

## Form-behavior

- [data-autosave](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-autosave/): Save form drafts to localStorage as the user types and restore them on the next visit. Skips passwords, hidden inputs, buttons and card or one-time codes. Clears on submit or reset; drafts expire after 24 hours.
- [data-count](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-count/): Live character or word count under a textarea, with warning and error states near and over the limit and polite screen-reader announcements.
- [data-grow](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-grow/): Auto-expand a textarea as the user types, from its rows up to an optional data-max-rows cap. CSS field-sizing where supported, a JavaScript measuring fallback elsewhere.
- [data-select-all](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-select-all/): Master checkbox for bulk selection. Add data-select-all to a checkbox to control a group of related checkboxes, with indeterminate state, disabled items skipped and a live count.
- [data-show-when](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-show-when/): Show or hide a form section based on other fields' values. Hidden sections get hidden + inert and their controls are disabled, so hidden required fields never block submit and hidden values are not sent.
- [data-wizard](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-wizard/): Split a form into steps: per-step validation, conditional steps whose fields are disabled while skipped, Enter-to-advance, focus management, localisable labels, optional persistence and URL history. Add data-wizard to a form of fieldsets.

## Form-controls

- [data-accept](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-accept/): Character filter for text inputs: block characters outside a preset or custom character class while the user formats freely. Presets for phone, date, card numbers, letters and more.
- [data-color](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-color/): Show a native colour input as a round swatch with its hex code. The native input stays the only control; the swatch and text are decoration.
- [data-floating-label](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-floating-label/): Animated floating label that starts inside the input and moves above on focus or when filled. Material Design pattern that keeps the label always visible.
- [data-loading](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-loading/): Button loading state with spinner, aria-busy, double-submit prevention, and auto-revert for async actions.
- [data-mask](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-mask/): Format a text input as the user types, from a preset (US phone, card, US date, SSN, ZIP) or your own pattern. Incomplete values are invalid, so required works.
- [data-range](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-range/): Styled range slider with a filled track, an optional value bubble, prefix/suffix and locale formatting, tick markers and datalist labels. Covers data-range, data-bubble, data-prefix, data-suffix and data-markers.
- [data-segmented](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-segmented/): Group radio inputs into a compact segmented control with sunken track and raised active segment. CSS-only pattern over native radios with vertical and compact variants.
- [data-stepper](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-stepper/): Visible − and + buttons for a native number input. Steps exactly like the arrow keys, follows disabled and readonly, and re-syncs after a form reset.
- [data-strength](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-strength/): Password strength meter and rules checklist for a password input inside form-field. Advisory by default; data-strength-min makes weak passwords invalid.
- [data-switch](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-switch/): Style a native checkbox as an on/off toggle switch, in three sizes. The look is pure CSS; a small script adds role='switch'.
- [data-toggle-tags](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-toggle-tags/): Style a fieldset of checkboxes as selectable pill chips. Pure CSS; data-max adds a small script that caps the selection and announces the limit.
- [data-upload](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-upload/): Turn a native file input into a drag-and-drop zone with a file list. Dropped files follow the input's accept and multiple rules; rejected files are announced.
- [data-vb-email-form](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-vb-email-form/): Submit any HTML form through VBService('email') using a named template. Progressive enhancement on top of native form action.
- [data-vb-newsletter-form](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-vb-newsletter-form/): Newsletter signup, unsubscribe, and preferences forms wired through VBService('newsletter'). Progressive enhancement on top of native form action.

## Formatting

- [data-format-bytes](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-format-bytes/): Human-readable file size formatting. Add data-format-bytes to any &lt;data&gt; element for automatic byte formatting.
- [data-format-date](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-format-date/): Locale-aware date and relative time formatting via data attributes.
- [data-format-number](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-format-number/): Locale-aware number formatting using Intl.NumberFormat. Add data-format-number to any &lt;data&gt; element for automatic formatting.
- [data-math](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-math/): Enhance code elements with precompiled MathML rendering. Add data-math to any code element for automatic MathML injection with numbering, copy, and Markdown integration.
- [data-ticker](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-ticker/): Removed. Animated count-up is now data-effect='ticker' — see the data-effect page.

## Infrastructure

- [data-print](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-print/): Print optimization attributes for controlling how pages look when printed — page modes, element visibility, page breaks, and opt-out.
- [data-toc-ignore](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-toc-ignore/): Leave a heading, or every heading in a container, out of the page-toc table of contents and the heading-links anchor links.
- [hide-until-ready](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/hide-until-ready/): CSS-only FOUC guards for custom elements: hide an element until its definition loads (with a no-JS and timeout escape), or show placeholder content until then.
- [view-transitions](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/view-transitions/): Cross-page (MPA) view transitions: an opt-in stylesheet, named groups, shared element morphing, animation presets, and a declarative init script.

## Interaction

- [data-effect="animate-image"](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-animate-image/): Play/pause control for animated images. Add data-effect='animate-image' to any GIF, WebP or APNG for a pause button that really stops the animation, reduced-motion support and picture/srcset support.
- [data-audio-playlist](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-audio-playlist/): Turns a native audio element and a list of track links into a playlist: click a track to play it, finished tracks are marked, and playback moves to the next track.
- [data-hotkey](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-hotkey/): Platform-aware keyboard shortcut display and declarative action binding. On &lt;kbd&gt; elements renders platform symbols; on other elements binds keyboard shortcuts to actions, honouring the user's single-key shortcut preference (WCAG 2.1.4).
- [data-markdown-editable](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-markdown-editable/): Inline markdown editing on any text element: raw markdown while focused, sanitised formatting after blur. On a textarea or input it renders a preview instead.
- [data-splitter](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-splitter/): Add a resizable drag divider between panels with keyboard support. The lightweight attribute alternative to the full split-surface web component.
- [data-spoiler](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-spoiler/): Hide content behind blur, solid, or noise overlays until the reader chooses to reveal it. Works on any element, keeps its semantics, and supports keyboard, screen readers, localisation and print.
- [data-toggle](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-toggle/): Click-to-flip-attribute upscale. Toggles a boolean attribute, ARIA two-state value, custom on/off value, or CSS class on a target — the catch-all for the recurring 'change state' pattern that doesn't have a native primitive.

## Layout

- [data-canvas](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-canvas/): Turn any semantic element into an elevated surface: background, 1px edge, radius, shadow, padding and a centred max width. The attribute form of &lt;layout-canvas&gt;.
- [data-container](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-container/): Make any element a CSS size-query container (container-type: inline-size), optionally named card, panel or media, and keep sectioning children of content-sized layouts as containers on purpose.
- [data-layout-density](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-layout-density/): Region-wide density variant. Set on &lt;html&gt;, &lt;body&gt; or any container to swap the VB spacing scale (--size-3xs through --size-3xl) for a tighter or looser one, without touching individual layouts. Compact for dashboards and admin UIs, spacious for marketing pages.
- [data-layout](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-layout/): Component-level layout primitive. Drop on any element to apply a named layout (stack, cluster, grid, center, cover, sidebar, columns…) without wrapping in a custom element. Same surface as the layout-* custom elements; better semantics.
- [data-page-layout](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-page-layout/): VB's page-template system. Put it on &lt;body&gt; and the semantic children (header, nav, main, aside, footer) auto-assign to named grid areas: no classes, no wrappers. Eight templates, sidebar width and gap modifiers, mobile collapse and an accessible dashboard drawer.
- [data-paged](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-paged/): Pagination upscale for any list-shaped container — native ul/ol/table or VB collections like card-list, data-table, layout-grid. Numbered, prev/next, load-more, and infinite styles. Optional URL state.
- [data-stage](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-stage/): Scrollytelling layout pattern: pinned visual on one side, sequential semantic steps on the other. Pure CSS, no scroll listeners.
- [data-sticky](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-sticky/): Sticky page chrome. On &lt;header&gt; or &lt;footer&gt; it pins the element on its own; on &lt;html&gt; it switches on the coordination system, which measures the sticky header into --sticky-offset so sticky sidebars, the TOC and anchor jumps all line up below it.

## Media

- [data-responsive](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-responsive/): Responsive image helper: measures an image's rendered width into sizes, generates srcset from a widths shorthand, and shows an optional dev badge naming the selected source.

## Native

- [accept](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/accept/): Tells a file input which file types to offer, by extension or MIME type. It filters the picker but is only a hint; Vanilla Breeze's data-upload applies the same rules to dropped files.
- [accesskey](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/accesskey/): Assigns a browser keyboard shortcut (modifier plus one key) that focuses or activates an element. Hard to discover and prone to clashes; VB's data-hotkey is usually the better choice.
- [allow](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/allow/): Sets an iframe's Permissions Policy: which powerful features (camera, microphone, fullscreen, payment, geolocation) the embedded document may use.
- [ARIA states](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/aria-states/): The ARIA state attributes Vanilla Breeze styles or sets: aria-current, aria-pressed, aria-expanded, aria-disabled, aria-busy, aria-invalid, aria-sort, aria-selected and aria-keyshortcuts.
- [async / defer](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/async-defer/): Control when external scripts download and run relative to HTML parsing: blocking, async, defer, and type=module, which is deferred by default.
- [autocapitalize](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/autocapitalize/): Hints how virtual keyboards and voice input capitalize typed text: none, sentences, words or characters. Set it on a field or on its form.
- [autocomplete](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/autocomplete/): Tells the browser and password managers what a field holds, so saved names, addresses, cards, passwords and one-time codes can be filled in one step.
- [autocorrect](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/autocorrect/): Turns the browser's or operating system's automatic spelling and punctuation correction on or off for editable text. Baseline 2026; inherited from the form.
- [autofocus](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/autofocus/): Focuses an element when the page loads, or when its dialog or popover opens. The first focusable autofocus element in each scope wins.
- [blocking](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/blocking/): Marks a resource that would not block on its own (a module, async or script-inserted resource) as render-blocking, so the browser does not paint until it loads.
- [cite](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/cite/): A machine-readable source URL for quotations and edits on blockquote, q, del and ins. Browsers never show it, so pair it with visible attribution.
- [class](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/class/): VB uses classes for named, element-scoped variants (button.secondary, nav.pills, header.site). State and configuration live in data-* attributes instead.
- [commandfor](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/commandfor/): Declarative invoker buttons: commandfor names a target and command says what to do to it, opening dialogs and popovers or firing your own commands without click handlers.
- [contenteditable](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/contenteditable/): Let users edit an element's content in place, as rich text or plain text only. Covers the roles and labels you must add, sanitising saved HTML, and VB's markdown-editable enhancement.
- [controls](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/controls/): Show the browser's built-in play, seek and volume controls on audio and video, or hand the job to VB's video-player and audio-player components.
- [crossorigin](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/crossorigin/): Fetches a script, stylesheet, image or media file in CORS mode, which SRI, font preloads, canvas pixel access and full script error details all depend on.
- [datetime](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/datetime/): A machine-readable date, time or duration on time, del and ins, while the visible text stays human-friendly. VB's data-format-date formats it for you.
- [dir](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/dir/): Sets the base text direction (ltr, rtl or auto). Needed for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu; VB mirrors direction-specific UI through :dir(rtl).
- [dirname](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/dirname/): Submits the text direction of a field (ltr or rtl) as an extra form value, so the server can display user-written text in the direction it was typed.
- [disabled](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/disabled/): Turns a form control off: it can't be focused, edited or activated, it is skipped by validation, and its value is not submitted. On a fieldset it disables every control inside.
- [download](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/download/): Makes a link save its target as a file instead of navigating to it, optionally suggesting a file name. Works for same-origin, blob: and data: URLs.
- [draggable](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/draggable/): Make an element draggable with the HTML Drag and Drop API. Covers the default auto state, the event lifecycle, VB's drag state styling hooks, and the keyboard and single-pointer alternatives every drag needs.
- [enterkeyhint](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/enterkeyhint/): Sets the label or icon on the Enter key of a touch keyboard (Next, Done, Go, Search, Send). It only changes the label; what Enter does is still up to the form or your script.
- [form](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/form/): Associates a form control with a form by id, so the control can sit anywhere in the document and still be validated, reset and submitted with that form.
- [formaction](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/formaction/): Per-button submission overrides: formaction, formmethod, formenctype, formtarget and formnovalidate let one form send to different URLs, in different ways, depending on the button pressed.
- [hidden](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/hidden/): Mark content as not relevant right now so it is not rendered, focusable or announced, or use hidden='until-found' to collapse it while find-in-page can still reveal it.
- [inert](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/inert/): Make a subtree unusable: no focus, no clicks, no text selection and hidden from screen readers, while it stays on screen. Covers what inert does not do, and how it differs from hidden and disabled.
- [inputmode](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/inputmode/): Chooses which on-screen keyboard a touch device shows for a field (numeric, decimal, tel, email, url, search or none) without changing the field's type or validation.
- [integrity](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/integrity/): Subresource Integrity: give a script or stylesheet the hash of the exact file you expect, and the browser refuses to use anything else.
- [interestfor](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/interestfor/): Open a popover when the user hovers or focuses a button or link. Covers popover='hint' tooltips, delays, events, and the polyfill Vanilla Breeze ships for browsers without it.
- [is](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/is/): Upgrades a native element into a customized built-in element that keeps its native semantics. Not supported in Safari; VB gets the same result with data-* enhancers.
- [lang](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/lang/): Declares the language of content with a BCP 47 tag. Drives screen-reader pronunciation, and in VB also quotation marks, script typography, hyphenation and number and date formatting.
- [list](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/list/): Connects an input to a datalist of suggested values. The user can pick a suggestion or type anything else; on range, colour and date inputs the options become marks and swatches.
- [loading](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/loading/): Lazy loading, fetch priority and image decoding hints: three attributes that decide when and how urgently the browser fetches images, iframes and scripts.
- [min / max / step](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/min-max-step/): Range and increment constraints for number, range, date and time inputs. Covers step bases, step='any', the range defaults and Vanilla Breeze's stepper and slider enhancements.
- [minlength / maxlength](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/minlength-maxlength/): Length limits for text fields and textareas: maxlength stops typing at the limit, minlength makes a too-short value invalid. Vanilla Breeze adds a live counter and custom messages.
- [multiple](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/multiple/): Lets a select, an email input or a file input hold more than one value. Covers select size, the email list format and how each control submits its values.
- [nonce](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/nonce/): A one-time token that marks a script or style as trusted under Content Security Policy. Put it on every script you serve, inline or external, and pair it with 'strict-dynamic'.
- [novalidate](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/novalidate/): Turns off the browser's submit-time validation for a whole form (novalidate) or for one submit button (formnovalidate). Constraints still apply; only the blocking and the bubbles stop.
- [open](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/open/): The boolean state attribute of details and dialog: whether a disclosure is expanded or a dialog is showing. Covers exclusive accordions, modal versus non-modal dialogs, closedby, and VB's open and close animation.
- [pattern](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/pattern/): Validates a text input's value against a regular expression. The whole value must match, the pattern is compiled with the v flag, and an empty optional field is always valid.
- [ping](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/ping/): Hyperlink auditing: when a link is followed, the browser POSTs a small notification to each listed URL while it navigates. Firefox ignores it by default.
- [placeholder](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/placeholder/): Shows a short hint inside an empty field, such as an example of the expected format. It is not a label and it disappears as soon as the user types.
- [popover](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/popover/): Turn any element into a top-layer popover with light dismiss. Covers auto, manual and hint popovers, how to open them, and what Vanilla Breeze does and does not style.
- [poster](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/poster/): The image a video shows before playback starts. Pairs with preload=none for bandwidth savings; VB players and data-mock set it for you.
- [preload](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/preload/): Hint how much of an audio or video file to download before play: none, metadata or auto. Trades bandwidth against how fast playback starts.
- [readonly](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/readonly/): Makes a text-like field non-editable while keeping it focusable, selectable and submitted. Vanilla Breeze gives read-only fields a sunken fill and a dashed border.
- [referrerpolicy](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/referrerpolicy/): Sets how much of the current page's URL is sent as the Referer when an element fetches a resource or follows a link.
- [rel](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/rel/): Says how a linked resource relates to the page: stylesheets and resource hints on link, opener and referrer control on links and forms, and meaning that VB styles.
- [required](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/required/): Marks a form control that must have a value before its form can be submitted. Works without JavaScript; Vanilla Breeze adds the asterisk, the error styling and custom messages.
- [reversed](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/reversed/): Ordered-list numbering: reversed counts down, start sets the first number, li value jumps the count, and type picks the marker. VB widens the indent for long markers.
- [sandbox](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/sandbox/): Locks down an iframe: scripts, forms, popups, top-level navigation and the frame's real origin are all withheld until you add tokens to grant them back.
- [spellcheck](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/spellcheck/): Turns the browser's spell-checker on or off for editable text. Inherits from ancestors; turn it off for code, identifiers and sensitive fields.
- [srcdoc](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/srcdoc/): Gives an iframe an inline HTML document instead of a URL. Without sandbox the document runs with your page's origin, so untrusted HTML always needs sandbox.
- [srcset](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/srcset/): Offer several image files so the browser picks the right one for the layout width and pixel density. Covers sizes, sizes=auto, picture and VB's data-responsive.
- [tabindex](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/tabindex/): Makes an element focusable and sets its place in the Tab order. Use 0 for a focus stop, -1 for script-only focus, and never a positive number.
- [target](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/target/): Chooses where a link or form result opens: the same tab, a new tab, a parent or top-level frame, or a named window or iframe.
- [title](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/title/): Advisory text shown as a mouse-hover tooltip and used as an accessible name or description. Good for abbr and iframe; never the only place for important text.
- [translate](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/translate/): Marks text and translatable attribute values that machine translation must leave alone: code, brand names, identifiers. Inherited; empty means yes.
- [wrap](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/wrap/): Controls whether a textarea's submitted value gets line breaks where the text wraps on screen (hard) or only where the user pressed Enter (soft, the default).

## Prototyping

- [data-lorem](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-lorem/): Placeholder text via data attributes. Fill any element with lorem ipsum, specify word counts, sentence counts, or list items. Auto-detects language for Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew and Cyrillic corpuses.
- [data-mock](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-mock/): Placeholder media via data attributes. Add data-mock to img, video, iframe, or canvas for instant placeholder boxes with X-pattern, presets, and photo service integration.
- [data-wireframe](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-wireframe/): Wireframe mode for rapid HTML prototyping. Apply sketch-like rendering with four fidelity levels, dark mode support, and element labeling via a single data attribute.

## Responsive

- [data-visible](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-visible/): Responsive visibility utility. Show or hide elements by viewport width or by the width of their container, without writing custom media or container queries.

## Shapes

- [data-border-shape](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-border-shape/): A coloured hexagon, diamond or arch frame around an image: a clipped background layer plus the image clipped to the same shape, inset by --shape-border.
- [data-bubble](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-bubble/): Chat bubble shapes for messaging UIs: incoming, outgoing, assistant, thought, typing, error and system variants with CSS shape() tails that mirror in right-to-left text.
- [data-callout](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-callout/): VB's one callout primitive: note, info, tip, warning and danger boxes, with optional speech and notched shapes. markdown-viewer renders :::kind blocks with the same markup.
- [data-clip](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-clip/): Responsive shape masks for images and figures using CSS shape(): hexagon, arch, swoosh, leaf, diagonal-frame, torn.
- [data-cutout](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-cutout/): Punch a circle, diamond, arch window or hexagon hole through an element, or bite its top corner, with an evenodd CSS shape().
- [data-morph](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-morph/): Animate an element's clip-path between matching shapes: pulse, breathe, wave. One cycle by default; data-morph-loop loops with pause on hover, focus, data-paused and reduced motion.
- [data-shape-start](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-shape-start/): Section edges: clip the top or bottom edge of a section into a wave, chevron, scallop or diagonal with CSS shape(). Any start shape combines with any end shape.

## Text-effects

- [data-effect](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-effect/): Declarative visual effects: entrances, attention seekers, decorations, exits and text effects through one attribute. Composable animation slots, triggers, reduced-motion and pause support.
- [data-emoji](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-emoji/): Replace :shortcode: text with Unicode emoji in containers, accessible-name attributes and live in inputs. Without JavaScript, shortcodes stay as readable text.

## Visual-effects

- [data-parallax](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-parallax/): Section-local, transform-only depth motion driven by a CSS view-progress timeline. CSS-only, clipped by its group, and off under either reduced-motion switch.
- [data-stagger](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-stagger/): Cascades entrance timing across a container's children: linear, reverse, random or a grid wave, with an optional interval such as 40ms.
- [data-transition](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-transition/): Declarative View Transitions for same-document changes: morph, slide (writing-direction aware), fade, scale, a staggered list and none, animated by VB.swap() or any component transition.
- [data-trigger](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/attributes/data-trigger/): Controls when a data-effect activates: on scroll, hover or focus, click, after a delay, on a media query, an event, a view transition, or continuously with scroll position.

---

# Vanilla Breeze 0.7.4: native elements

Native HTML elements are styled with no classes. These pages document the variants and attributes Vanilla Breeze adds to each.

## Document

- [<base>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/base/): Sets the base URL that every relative URL in the document resolves against, and a default target for links and forms.
- [<body>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/body/): The document's content: the container for every landmark on the page and the surface VB paints the page background on.
- [<head>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/head/): The configuration surface for metadata, theming, performance, and social sharing.
- [<html>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/html/): The root element of an HTML document, containing all other elements.
- [<link>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/link/): Connects the document to external resources: stylesheets, icons, preload and preconnect hints, and machine-readable relations such as canonical, author and license.
- [<meta>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/meta/): Document metadata that no other head element covers: character encoding, viewport, description, theme colour, pragma directives, and the metadata VB components read.
- [<style>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/style/): Embeds a CSS stylesheet in the document. Covers cascade-layer placement against VB's layers, media-scoped blocks, CSP nonces, render blocking, and why a style block or tokens beat style attributes.
- [<title>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/title/): Defines the document title shown in browser tabs, bookmarks, history, search results, and screen reader announcements.

## Editing

- [<del>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/del/): The del element represents text that has been deleted from a document, typically displayed with a strikethrough and red background tint for tracking edits or showing revisions.
- [<ins>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/ins/): The ins element represents text that has been inserted into a document, styled with a green bottom border and subtle green background for tracking edits or showing revisions.

## Embedded

- [<canvas>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/canvas/): The canvas element provides a drawing surface for rendering graphics, charts, games, and dynamic visual content via JavaScript.
- [<embed>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/embed/): The embed element is a void element for embedding external content. It provides no fallback mechanism -- prefer modern alternatives like iframe, video, and audio.
- [<iframe>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/iframe/): The iframe element embeds external content with responsive containers and security best practices for third-party integrations.
- [<math>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/math/): Native MathML rendering with a self-hosted math font, display and inline modes, numbered and captioned equations.
- [<object>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/object/): The object element is a legacy mechanism for embedding external resources. Modern alternatives like img, video, audio, iframe, and svg are preferred.
- [<svg>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/svg/): The SVG element embeds scalable vector graphics with size variants, color options, and built-in animations for icons and illustrations.

## Forms

- [<button>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/button/): Interactive control for form submission, dialogs, and user actions. Vanilla Breeze styles buttons with inline-flex layout, design tokens, and variant classes for visual hierarchy.
- [<datalist>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/datalist/): Provides autocomplete suggestions for input elements. The datalist creates a native dropdown of options that users can select from while still allowing free-form text entry.
- [<fieldset>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/fieldset/): Groups related form controls together with an optional caption. Essential for organizing complex forms and providing accessible groupings for screen readers.
- [<form>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/form/): Container for interactive form controls that collects and submits user data. The form element provides structure, validation, and submission handling.
- [<input>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/input/): The most versatile form element, accepting text, numbers, dates, files, and more through the type attribute. Always pair with a label for accessibility.
- [<label>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/label/): Associates a text caption with a form control. Labels are essential for accessibility, enabling screen readers to announce form fields and allowing users to click the label to focus the associated input.
- [<legend>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/legend/): Provides a caption for a fieldset element. The legend is announced by screen readers as the group's label, making it essential for accessibility.
- [<meter>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/meter/): Displays a scalar measurement within a known range, like a gauge. The meter automatically changes color based on whether the value is in the optimum, suboptimum, or poor range.
- [<optgroup>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/optgroup/): Groups related options within a select element under a visible label. Helps users scan long option lists organized into logical categories.
- [<option>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/option/): Defines an item in a select dropdown or datalist autocomplete. Each option has a value submitted to the server and display text shown to the user.
- [<output>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/output/): Displays the result of a calculation or user action. Semantically ideal for form validation messages, computed values, and dynamic results. Used extensively in the form-field custom element for validation feedback.
- [<progress>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/progress/): Displays the completion progress of a task. Use for file uploads, form steps, loading states, or any operation with a known endpoint. For scalar measurements (like disk space), use meter instead.
- [<search>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/search/): Semantic landmark element for search functionality. Wraps search forms and controls to provide accessibility and structural meaning.
- [<select>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/select/): Dropdown menu for choosing from a list of predefined options. Vanilla Breeze resets the native appearance and adds a currentColor chevron, consistent sizing, and focus styling via design tokens.
- [<selectedcontent>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/selectedcontent/): Displays a clone of the currently selected option's content inside a customizable select's button trigger. Used with appearance: base-select to show rich content (icons, images, descriptions) in the closed select state.
- [<textarea>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/textarea/): Multi-line text input for longer content like messages, comments, or descriptions. Unlike input type='text', textarea allows line breaks and resizing.

## Headings

- [<headings>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/headings/): Heading elements define the hierarchical structure of a document. Six levels from h1 (most important) to h6 (least), used for titles, sections, and content organization.

## Interactive

- [<details>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/details/): The native HTML disclosure widget for expandable content. Creates an interactive widget that users can open and close without JavaScript.
- [<dialog>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/dialog/): The native HTML modal dialog element with built-in backdrop, focus trapping, and keyboard handling.
- [<summary>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/summary/): The clickable heading for a details disclosure widget. Provides the visible label that toggles the expanded content.

## Lists

- [<dd>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/dd/): The definition description element provides the description, definition, or value associated with a term in a definition list.
- [<dl>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/dl/): The description list element represents a collection of term-description pairs, such as glossaries, metadata, or key-value data.
- [<dt>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/dt/): The definition term element represents the term, name, or key in a term-description group within a definition list.
- [<li>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/li/): The list item element represents an individual item within a list structure.
- [<menu>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/menu/): List container for toolbar buttons and context menu patterns. Groups related commands; exposed to assistive technology as a list.
- [<ol>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/ol/): The ordered list element represents a collection of items where the sequence is meaningful.
- [<ul>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/ul/): The unordered list element represents a collection of items where the sequence does not matter.

## Media

- [<area>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/area/): Defines a clickable region within a map element using pixel-based shape coordinates. Used with img and map for client-side image maps.
- [<audio>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/audio/): The audio element embeds sound content with native playback controls, styled variants, and an optional track listing for playlists.
- [<img>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/img/): The image element embeds responsive images with automatic sizing, lazy loading support, and visual variants for different use cases.
- [<map>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/map/): Defines an image map with clickable regions linked to an img element via the usemap attribute. Coordinates are pixel-based and do not scale responsively.
- [<picture>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/picture/): The picture element enables art direction and format switching by providing multiple image sources for different screen sizes and browser capabilities.
- [<source>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/source/): The source element specifies multiple media resources for picture, video, and audio elements, enabling format fallbacks and responsive media selection.
- [<track>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/track/): The track element provides timed text tracks for video and audio elements, enabling captions, subtitles, descriptions, and chapter markers.
- [<video>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/video/): The video element embeds video content with native playback controls, responsive sizing, and aspect ratio variants for different video formats.

## Scripting

- [<noscript>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/noscript/): Content that is used only when scripting is disabled. In VB, a supplement to progressive enhancement alongside data-requires-js and the (scripting: none) media query.
- [<script>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/script/): Loads or embeds JavaScript, or carries a data block such as JSON-LD or an import map. Covers classic vs module scripts, async/defer, render blocking, CSP nonces and integrity.
- [<slot>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/slot/): A placeholder inside a shadow root that shows the host's light-DOM children. Explains named and default slots, declarative shadow DOM, ::slotted, slotchange, and how VB's mostly light-DOM components use slot= as a styling hook.
- [<template>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/template/): Holds inert HTML that is parsed but not rendered. Covers cloning template.content, declarative shadow DOM with shadowrootmode, accessibility, and the VB components that read author templates.

## Sectioning

- [<address>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/address/): Contact information for the nearest article or document. Typically contains physical address, email, phone, or social links.
- [<article>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/article/): Self-contained, independently distributable content such as blog posts, news articles, forum posts, product cards, or user comments.
- [<aside>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/aside/): Content tangentially related to the surrounding content. Used for sidebars, pull quotes, and supplementary information boxes.
- [<footer>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/footer/): Footer content for its nearest sectioning ancestor. Contains information about the author, copyright, related links, or metadata about the section.
- [<header>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/header/): Introductory content for its nearest sectioning ancestor. Contains headings, logos, navigation, search forms, or other introductory elements.
- [<hgroup>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/hgroup/): Groups a heading with secondary content such as a subtitle, alternative title, or tagline. Creates a single logical heading unit.
- [<main>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/main/): The dominant content of the document body. Contains the primary content unique to the page, excluding headers, footers, navigation, and sidebars.
- [<nav>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/nav/): Navigation sections containing links to other pages or parts of the page. Used for primary navigation, table of contents, breadcrumbs, and pagination.
- [<section>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/section/): A thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading. Use for chapters, tabbed panels, numbered sections, or any content that would appear in an outline.

## Tables

- [<caption>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/caption/): Provides a title or description for a table. Vanilla Breeze styles captions with start-aligned text, muted color, and medium font weight to clearly label tabular data without competing with the data itself.
- [<col>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/col/): Defines properties for a single column or a span of columns within a colgroup. Use it to set column widths, apply background colors, or highlight specific columns in a table.
- [<colgroup>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/colgroup/): Groups one or more columns in a table for structural and styling purposes. Supports the span attribute for multi-column groups or individual col elements for per-column control.
- [<table>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/table/): Tables display tabular data with full-width layout, collapsed borders, tabular numerals, and automatic row hover states. Includes data-striped, data-bordered, data-density and minimal variants plus data attributes for density, alignment, sticky headers and columns, responsive card and scroll layouts, and row states.
- [<tbody>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/tbody/): The tbody element groups body rows of a table. Vanilla Breeze adds a hover highlight on rows and supports a striped variant for easier scanning.
- [<td>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/td/): The td element defines a data cell in a table. Vanilla Breeze styles cells with a thin bottom border and top vertical alignment. Supports data attributes for numeric alignment, custom sort/filter values, and responsive card-mode labels.
- [<tfoot>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/tfoot/): The tfoot element groups footer rows of a table. Vanilla Breeze styles it with bold text, a raised background, and a medium top border to visually distinguish summary rows from data.
- [<th>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/th/): The th element defines a header cell in a table. Vanilla Breeze styles headers with a raised background and semi-bold weight. Always use scope for accessibility. Supports sort indicators and numeric alignment via data attributes.
- [<thead>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/thead/): The thead element groups header rows in a table. Vanilla Breeze styles it with a raised background and a medium bottom border to visually separate column headers from data.
- [<tr>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/tr/): The tr element defines a row of cells in a table. Vanilla Breeze adds data attributes for row states like selection, highlighting, and expandable detail rows.

## Text Content

- [<blockquote>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/blockquote/): The blockquote element represents a section quoted from another source, with VB styling for figure-based attribution, prose refinement, and academic citation patterns.
- [<div>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/div/): Generic block-level container. In Vanilla Breeze, div usage is discouraged — prefer semantic elements and VB layout primitives.
- [<figcaption>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/figcaption/): The figcaption element provides a caption or legend for the content of its parent figure element.
- [<figure>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/figure/): The figure element represents self-contained content with an optional caption, used for images, diagrams, code snippets, and quotations.
- [<hr>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/hr/): The horizontal rule element represents a thematic break between paragraph-level content, signaling a shift in topic or scene.
- [<p>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/p/): The paragraph element represents a block of text, forming the basic building block of written content on the web.
- [<pre>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/pre/): Preformatted text preserving whitespace and line breaks. VB distinguishes code blocks (pre+code) from bare preformatted text (poetry, ASCII art) with different visual treatments.

## Text Semantics

- [<a>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/a/): The anchor element creates hyperlinks to web pages, files, email addresses, locations within the same page, or any other URL.
- [<abbr>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/abbr/): The abbreviation element represents an abbreviation or acronym, optionally with its expansion shown via the title attribute.
- [<b>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/b/): Draws attention to text without conveying extra importance. Used for keywords, product names, or lead text in article summaries.
- [<bdi>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/bdi/): Isolates text that might be formatted in a different direction from surrounding text.
- [<bdo>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/bdo/): Overrides the current text direction, forcing text to render left-to-right or right-to-left.
- [<br>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/br/): Produces a line break in text content. Use only where the line break is part of the content's meaning.
- [<cite>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/cite/): Represents the title of a creative work (book, song, film, etc.).
- [<code>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/code/): Elements for displaying code, keyboard input, sample output, and variables in technical documentation.
- [<data>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/data/): Links content with a machine-readable value. Enhanced in VB with locale-aware number formatting, byte formatting, and animated ticker effects.
- [<dfn>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/dfn/): The dfn element indicates the defining instance of a term, marking where a term is first introduced and defined in the document.
- [<em>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/em/): Marks text with stress emphasis that changes the meaning of a sentence. Rendered as italic, with synthesized italic as a fallback.
- [<i>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/i/): Represents text in an alternate voice, mood, or language — foreign words, technical terms, thoughts, ship names, or taxonomic designations.
- [<kbd>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/kbd/): The kbd element represents user keyboard input, displaying keys and key combinations in a distinctive style that resembles physical keyboard keys.
- [<mark>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/mark/): The mark element represents text highlighted for its relevance in context, with VB highlight categories (success, warning, error) that stay readable in light, dark and forced-colors modes.
- [<q>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/q/): Represents an inline quotation with locale-aware quotation marks via VB's i18n system.
- [<rp>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/rp/): Provides fallback parentheses for browsers that do not support ruby annotations.
- [<rt>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/rt/): Specifies the ruby text (annotation) in a ruby annotation, providing pronunciation or other guidance above base text.
- [<ruby>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/ruby/): Represents a ruby annotation, used for East Asian typography to show pronunciation guides above or beside base text.
- [<s>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/s/): The s element represents content that is no longer accurate or no longer relevant, displayed with a strikethrough line.
- [<samp>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/samp/): Represents sample or quoted output from a computer program. Rendered in monospace font.
- [<small>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/small/): Represents side comments, disclaimers, caveats, and fine print. Rendered at a smaller font size.
- [<span>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/span/): Generic inline container for phrasing content. Use only when no semantic element fits — for effects, status indicators, translation control, or accessibility helpers.
- [<strong>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/strong/): Indicates strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Rendered at weight 600, with synthesised bold as a fallback for single-weight fonts.
- [<sub>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/sub/): Represents subscript text for chemical formulas, mathematical notation, and variable subscripts. Rendered smaller and below the baseline in any font.
- [<sup>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/sup/): Represents superscript text for exponents, ordinals, footnotes, and trademark symbols. Rendered smaller and raised in any font.
- [<time>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/time/): The time element represents a specific period in time, providing a machine-readable datetime value while displaying a human-readable format to users.
- [<u>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/u/): Represents an unarticulated annotation — typically spelling errors or Chinese proper names. Vanilla Breeze draws a wavy error-coloured underline, and a plain solid underline in Chinese, Japanese and Korean text.
- [<var>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/var/): Represents a variable in mathematics or programming, set in italic (upright with a dashed underline in Chinese, Japanese and Korean text).
- [<wbr>](https://vanilla-breeze.com/docs/elements/native/wbr/): Suggests a word break opportunity — the browser may break the line here if needed, but won't force a break.
